events.title: THE STONE’S SECOND APPOINTMENT
events.text: {{other}} remembers selling you the heated healing stone. It has, the seller explains, used up its medicinal warmth and requires a fresh fee.

choices.label: Decline to pay for the same fire twice

outcome.text: You keep your money and damage {{other}}’s confidence in repeat business.

choices.label: Show the stone to the waiting customers

outcome.text: You expose the sales trick, gain public standing and make {{other}} a rival who remembers your first purchase less fondly.

events.title: THE RUMOUR’S NEW PRICE
events.text: {{other}} returns to the silence you bought. Its new price is announced loudly enough to explain what the first bargain was worth.

choices.label: Refuse the second payment

outcome.text: You keep the coin and lose more of {{other}}’s trust. The rivalry now has a clear financial history.

choices.label: Admit the original payment publicly

outcome.text: You disclose your part in the bargain and improve your own reputation. {{other}} acquires a rival who is no longer protecting the same secret.

events.title: THE ANCESTOR’S OTHER DESCENDANTS
events.text: {{other}} has sold a similar pedigree to a second household. Your shared ancestor has suddenly become more productive than any surviving record suggests.

choices.label: Withdraw your claim before it becomes testimony

outcome.text: You lose some family standing and keep the disagreement from producing a fresh lie. {{other}} resents an ancestor being returned.

choices.label: Defend the invented descent under oath

outcome.text: You add a genuine perjury charge to a false family history. {{other}} is now a named witness to the origin of the pedigree.

charge.offence: Defending an invented pedigree under oath

events.title: THE SCOOP’S NEW WITNESS
events.text: {{other}} still remembers your challenge to the milling measure. Another household asks whether you will repeat it before witnesses this time.

choices.label: Repeat only what you actually observed

outcome.text: You gain Commons standing and lose {{other}}’s affection. The dispute has acquired an honest witness rather than a larger story.

choices.label: Decline to enlarge the old quarrel

outcome.text: You preserve your time and lose a little public standing. {{other}} regards your silence as a useful, temporary arrangement.

events.title: THE PEDLAR’S LESS ANGELIC STOCK
events.text: {{other}} returns after your argument over the feather, now selling ordinary quills. The prices still suggest a distinguished ancestry.

choices.label: Welcome the honest description

outcome.text: You improve the acquaintance and gain Church standing. {{other}} is allowed to make a living without making an angel.

choices.label: Retell the old scandal for the new customers

outcome.text: You gain a little charm and turn a possible reform into a continuing rivalry.

events.title: THE LETTER YOUR INFORMANT KEPT
events.text: {{other}} has kept a copy of the accusation you helped deliver against the plotters. A useful letter, the holder explains, should not be allowed to retire.

choices.label: Publicly stand by what you actually reported

outcome.text: Your reputation falls under renewed attention, but you refuse a new secret bargain. {{other}} loses leverage over your silence.

choices.label: Pay for the copy without trusting it is the only one (12g)

outcome.text: You pay twelve gold for one copy and gain no promise that the rest have vanished. {{other}} finds your caution less profitable than your secrecy.

events.title: THE MIRACLE’S ACCOUNT BOOK
events.text: {{other}} asks how the donations attracted by your supposed miracle were used. The account needs figures rather than another account of the miracle.

choices.label: Fund visible relief (8g)

outcome.text: You fund actual relief, improve food security and gain Church standing. {{other}} accepts an answer that somebody can eat.

choices.label: Claim that the giving itself was sufficient

outcome.text: You lose trust and family standing by refusing an account. The original child’s recovery has not supplied a receipt.

events.title: THE COLLECTOR WITHOUT A PRINCIPAL
events.text: {{other}} remembers the lunch collection you resisted. The miller’s big son is absent; the smaller collector asks whether the old quarrel must continue without him.

choices.label: Accept a truce without pretending to be friends

outcome.text: You improve trust with {{other}}. The rivalry is not erased by a speech, but the next meeting need not collect another grievance.

choices.label: Demand lunch in repayment

outcome.text: You deepen the rivalry and lose a little reputation. {{other}} recognises the collection method immediately.

events.title: THE FEE YOUR MOTHER REMEMBERS
events.text: {{other}} has recovered enough to discuss the money spent during the fever. The question is less about the sum than whether you will ever stop reminding her of it.

choices.label: Tell her the account is closed between you

outcome.text: You deepen trust without erasing any actual loan. {{other}} relaxes into a conversation that is finally about something else.

choices.label: List everything you sacrificed

outcome.text: You keep the list and damage the bond. {{other}} is alive to hear it, which makes the account no kinder.

events.title: THE GLOVE LEFT IN A POCKET
events.text: Roderick remembers losing the argument instead of the duel. {{other}} has brought no glove this time, but has rehearsed an opening sentence.

choices.label: Hear the grievance without staging another victory

outcome.text: You hear {{other}} out without inviting the neighbours to enjoy it. The grievance becomes easier to understand when nobody is performing it.

choices.label: Repeat the winning argument in public

outcome.text: You gain charm and deepen the rivalry. {{other}} now has a second date to attach to the same grievance.

events.title: THE DECEASED OBJECTS AGAIN
events.text: {{other}} has received a copy of the corrected claim. Your parent asks whether being officially alive now excuses the next assessment.

choices.label: Explain that the victory restored ordinary obligations

outcome.text: You improve trust by refusing to turn one honest correction into another convenient fiction.

choices.label: Help meet the assessment (6g)

outcome.text: You contribute toward the household assessment. {{other}} agrees that life is expensive but preferable to the earlier paperwork.

events.title: THE WITHDRAWN CLAIM’S STORAGE FEE
events.text: {{other}} remembers the nine gold you paid to withdraw the false death claim. A new fee is proposed for storing the withdrawn document.

choices.label: Contest the second demand openly

outcome.text: You gain local reputation and make {{other}} a rival. The document has become expensive to keep hidden.

choices.label: Pay four gold to avoid another day in court

outcome.text: You spend four gold on delay rather than on a lasting settlement. {{other}} remembers which part of the first demand worked.

events.title: THE WEIGHT OF THE SALT CELLAR
events.text: {{other}} has found the missing household savings you took. The salt was weighed, which makes your explanation about rats particularly unhelpful.

choices.label: Restore twelve gold to the household (12g)

outcome.text: You replace the money and regain some trust. {{other}} does not have to pretend the loss was imaginary.

choices.label: Keep denying a loss that has been counted

outcome.text: You lose more trust and deepen the family quarrel. The unchanged cellar has become a very patient witness.

events.title: THE GUARANTEE’S FIRST ANNIVERSARY
events.text: {{other}} remembers the debt you accepted after the false guarantee. The promised contribution has not materialised; the explanation has improved substantially.

choices.label: Set clear terms for future help

outcome.text: You improve your own judgement and lose some of {{other}}’s affection. Existing debt remains real until paid.

choices.label: Keep the family bond without making a new promise

outcome.text: You preserve trust while refusing another guarantee. {{other}} learns that affection need not include an empty signature line.

events.title: THE QUESTION NO LONGER ASKED
events.text: {{other}} has stopped asking about the goods you concealed. The silence is obedient in exactly the way you once demanded.

choices.label: Admit that threatening the witness was wrong

outcome.text: You regain some trust by acknowledging the threat. The old evidence and any charges are not wiped away by the apology.

choices.label: Praise the silence and demand it continue

outcome.text: You deepen the damage to trust. {{other}} learns another lesson about what you call loyalty.

events.title: THE SEAL LEFT A GOOD IMPRESSION
events.text: {{other}} has been asked about the advance obtained with the soap seal. The seal has dissolved; the impression on the agreement has not.

choices.label: Give an honest account of the forgery

outcome.text: You gain some reputation for candour without removing the existing charge. {{other}} trusts the admission more than the earlier plan.

choices.label: Invent another document to support the first

outcome.text: You add a second forgery charge. {{other}} now has a much more complicated account to remember.

charge.offence: Creating false evidence for the soap-seal advance

events.title: THE GOODS LEFT AFTER THE LIST
events.text: {{other}} returns to discuss a small item omitted when your marriage ended. Both of you have brought the old inventory and a newer caution.

choices.label: Give up the disputed household item

outcome.text: Your household loses four gold of wealth and trust with {{other}} improves. The former marriage does not resume because an argument ends.

choices.label: Insist the silence in the list means ownership

outcome.text: You preserve the goods and deepen the quarrel. {{other}} adds a useful annotation to the old inventory.

events.title: THE JOKE REACHES THE OTHER DOOR
events.text: {{other}} hears the public joke you made about the suspected visits repeated back at home. It has acquired a kinder ending for everyone except your spouse.

choices.label: Correct your own story publicly

outcome.text: You regain some trust by taking the embarrassment yourself. {{other}} hears a difference between an apology and another joke.

choices.label: Insist that being hurt proves there was something to hide

outcome.text: You deepen the loss of trust. {{other}} is given a fresh accusation in place of an answer.

events.title: THE FOURTH WEDDING CREDITOR
events.text: {{other}} asks for the ten gold you took from the wedding reserve. The three brokers have become much less impressive as excuses for the fourth demand.

choices.label: Restore the ten gold (10g)

outcome.text: You replace the household money and recover some trust. {{other}} removes one name from the list of people awaiting payment.

choices.label: Keep the money and call it your fee

outcome.text: The family quarrel deepens. {{other}} now regards your help as something to budget against.

events.title: THE SINGER FINDS THE RIGHT WINDOW
events.text: {{other}} remembers your quiet correction of the storeroom serenade and offers to help you avoid a public embarrassment of your own.

choices.label: Accept the advice before making a speech

outcome.text: You gain charm and deepen the friendship. The favour is useful precisely because the audience never sees it happen.

choices.label: Trust your own judgement this time

outcome.text: You keep the decision your own and lose only a little of {{other}}’s enthusiasm for rescuing you.

events.title: THE SHADE OF AN OLD QUARREL
events.text: {{other}}’s household still remembers your family’s opposition to the shadow rent. A minor boundary question has arrived wearing the larger feud.

choices.label: Pay for a witnessed boundary discussion (11g)

outcome.text: You pay for mediation and improve trust. The existing family feud remains a real problem rather than disappearing into the refreshments.

choices.label: Answer with the old accusation

outcome.text: You deepen the quarrel and lower public order. {{other}} supplies the family with a fresh version of the grievance.

events.title: THE PARDON’S HANDWRITING
events.text: {{other}} is asked who filled in the blank pardon you presented. The missing seal is no longer the most interesting absence in the account.

choices.label: Give a truthful account without claiming a pardon

outcome.text: You improve your reputation a little. The forgery charge remains, and {{other}} is spared a second invented story.

choices.label: Blame the supplier for words you wrote

outcome.text: You damage trust with {{other}} and gain a rival who can identify your handwriting.

events.title: THE PIE’S UNHAPPY OWNER
events.text: {{other}} has not forgotten that you delivered the suggested verdict as evidence. The next meeting contains no pie and several extremely polite threats.

choices.label: Have the threats witnessed

outcome.text: You gain public standing by refusing to let the old evidence become a private bargain. {{other}} loses further trust in your discretion.

choices.label: End the meeting without a new bargain

outcome.text: You keep your record clear and the rivalry intact. {{other}} is left with the refreshments and the unsaid part of the threat.

events.title: THE MONEY AFTER THE MARK
events.text: {{other}} sees the arm injured by the substitute punishment and asks whether you would recommend the arrangement to someone else.

choices.label: Refuse to recruit a second substitute

outcome.text: You gain reputation and keep the chronic pain that made the offer real. {{other}} finds your endorsement unexpectedly unavailable.

choices.label: Ask for practical support rather than another bargain

outcome.text: You gain a little health and a more honest bond. The disability remains; the account of what it cost is less easy to evade.

events.title: THE UNCLE’S SECOND JOURNEY
events.text: {{other}} asks whether you will carry another supposed coffin. This one has ventilation holes and a much stricter request not to shake it.

choices.label: Refuse the second cargo

outcome.text: You keep clear of a new smuggling attempt and lose some of {{other}}’s favour. Your earlier record remains whatever it actually was.

choices.label: Require the cargo to be declared openly

outcome.text: You gain Crown standing by insisting on an honest declaration. {{other}} decides the route may be less profitable with you on it.

events.title: THE REHEARSAL’S NEXT AUDIENCE
events.text: {{other}}’s household remembers the rehearsed accusation you exposed. A new invitation has arrived, careful to contain no words that can easily be quoted.

choices.label: Refuse the invitation without inventing a threat

outcome.text: You preserve your distance and lose further affection. The household feud remains recorded rather than becoming a new conspiracy by assumption.

choices.label: Attend with witnesses of your own

outcome.text: You gain public standing through an openly witnessed meeting. {{other}} finds you difficult to invite into confidence.

events.title: THE BARRELS COME BACK FULL OF AIR
events.text: {{other}} returns with complaints about the false-measure barrels you signed. The workmanship has held up better than the description.

choices.label: Pay toward a correction (10g)

outcome.text: You spend ten gold and improve your working standing a little. The original fraud charge remains for the court.

choices.label: Defend the false capacity again

outcome.text: You deepen the loss of trust and professional standing. {{other}} has a barrel available for the demonstration.

events.title: THE CUSTOMER WHO KEPT THE RECALL
events.text: {{other}} remembers that you recalled the rejected goods at your own expense. A new customer asks whether your mark can be trusted.

choices.label: Ask for a plain account of the correction

outcome.text: You gain work performance and trust through the recommendation. The old mistake is included rather than hidden.

choices.label: Give the repairers their share of the credit

outcome.text: Your professional standing improves more broadly. {{other}} likes an account that makes room for the people who did the work.

events.title: THE BARGE’S VERY DRY DEBT
events.text: {{other}} brings the accounts of the venture you borrowed to fund. Whatever happened to the goods, the interest has remained perfectly sheltered.

choices.label: Review the real accounts before borrowing again

outcome.text: You gain work experience and a more cautious bond. No existing debt is cleared by understanding it better.

choices.label: Borrow another twelve gold against hoped-for returns

negative: A debt remains to be repaid

outcome.text: You add a twelve-gold obligation without creating an imaginary cargo. {{other}} finds the confidence encouraging.

events.title: THE PARTNER HAS FOUND A VOICE
events.text: {{other}} remembers your guarantee and proposes another. The earlier silence was evidently intended to leave room for this request.

choices.label: Refuse another guarantee while the first remains

outcome.text: You lose some favour and improve your judgement. Existing debt is not a qualification for acquiring more.

choices.label: Demand a full account before discussing terms

outcome.text: You gain work experience and a more exacting relationship. {{other}} has to turn the conversation from trust to figures.

events.title: THE WORD RETURNED TO THE CASE
events.text: {{other}}’s omitted “not” has been found in a retained draft. A single word now occupies most of the hearing.

choices.label: Provide the accurate draft

outcome.text: You gain a little reputation for candour and lose {{other}}’s trust. The original alteration remains a real charge.

choices.label: Try to destroy the retained draft

outcome.text: You add an evidence-destruction charge. The case now has two carefully named acts instead of one missing word.

charge.offence: Destroying evidence of a deliberately altered agreement

events.title: THE PATIENT WHO READ THE DATE
events.text: {{other}} has compared the certificate you sold with the day of the actual visit. Your former employment is being discussed in the past tense for a very definite reason.

choices.label: Acknowledge the false certificate

outcome.text: You gain some reputation for honesty without regaining the post or removing the charge. {{other}} finally receives an accurate statement.

choices.label: Insist that the date was clinically unimportant

outcome.text: You damage trust further. {{other}} regards the calendar as one of the few instruments used correctly in the case.

events.title: THE PATRON’S SAFER VERSE
events.text: {{other}} asks for another performance after you refused the accusation of treason. This time the proposed enemy is a badly maintained bridge.

choices.label: Accept a subject that cannot be imprisoned

outcome.text: You improve work performance and rebuild trust. The bridge is allowed no right of reply, but neither is it made into a person.

choices.label: Agree only to an honest account of the repair

outcome.text: You gain professional experience by writing within the facts. {{other}} learns that a commission can come with a conscience.

events.title: THE MEN WHO ARE ACTUALLY HERE
events.text: {{other}} brings the next muster list with the duplicate names crossed out. There are fewer men and far fewer explanations.

choices.label: Support the accurate muster

outcome.text: You improve Crown standing and rebuild trust. The smaller force is at least large enough to match its own account.

choices.label: Read out the earlier list for the company

outcome.text: You gain charm and deepen the rivalry. {{other}} discovers that correction has not bought discretion.

events.title: THE RING KEPT BY THE OTHER HOUSE
events.text: {{other}}’s household has kept the account of your accusation over the falcon. The old supper now appears whenever the families disagree about anything edible.

choices.label: Admit your false accusation

outcome.text: You improve trust at the cost of family standing. The recorded feud remains until the households actually find a way to repair it.

choices.label: Repeat the accusation for the new generation

outcome.text: You deepen the feud and lose public standing. {{other}} supplies another accurate account of what you have chosen to repeat.

events.title: THE RIVER AT THE HEARING
events.text: {{other}} has brought a corrected map after you demanded a survey. The river has resumed its inconvenient natural course.

choices.label: Accept the corrected evidence without a victory speech

outcome.text: You improve trust and gain Crown standing. {{other}} keeps enough dignity to continue using the accurate map.

choices.label: Make a public account of the earlier drawing

outcome.text: You gain reputation and damage the relationship. The corrected river now has to carry the old humiliation as well.

events.title: THE COIN RETURNS BY WEIGHT
events.text: {{other}} brings back the light coin issued under your order. Traders have begun weighing your face instead of trusting it.

choices.label: Fund a public correction (18g)

outcome.text: You spend personal gold to improve public order and family standing. The correction buys some goodwill; the charge over the dishonest issue remains on the roll.

choices.label: Blame the people weighing the coins

outcome.text: Public order falls further and {{other}} loses trust. The silver continues to be absent without asking anyone’s permission.

events.title: THE MORNING YOU REFUSED TO SAVE
events.text: {{other}} remembers your refusal to approve a condemnation before evidence. Another petition now arrives with witnesses rather than a convenient conclusion.

choices.label: Hear the better petition

outcome.text: You improve public order and rebuild trust. The earlier refusal has produced something more useful than an obedient morning.

choices.label: Require an ordinary hearing rather than a private favour

outcome.text: You gain Crown standing by keeping the decision out of a personal bargain. {{other}} accepts the limits reluctantly.

events.title: THE SAINT’S REVISED INVENTORY
events.text: {{other}} has removed the claim about the smaller skull. The new label says “object of uncertain history,” which is both less profitable and more defensible.

choices.label: Support the honest revision

outcome.text: You improve Church standing and trust with {{other}}. The object is allowed to remain interesting without another childhood.

choices.label: Keep telling the original joke

outcome.text: You gain a little charm and lose the chance to reward correction. {{other}} finds honesty a poor protection against your memory.

events.title: THE OVEN’S LESS CONVINCING WITNESS
events.text: {{other}} sees the lasting pain left by the burning ordeal. The oven has produced bread since, but no new evidence about your innocence.

choices.label: Explain publicly what the ordeal actually proved

outcome.text: You gain reputation by refusing to recommend the injury. The chronic pain remains a real cost rather than becoming proof of guilt.

choices.label: Accept practical help and rest

outcome.text: You recover some health and improve trust. Help eases the day without curing the disability.

events.title: THE SHORTER DONOR LIST
events.text: {{other}} has changed the distribution so food is served while names are read. Several donors object to not being heard over the grateful eating.

choices.label: Support the practical arrangement

outcome.text: You gain Church standing and deepen trust. The names still exist; they no longer have to be hungry first.

choices.label: Demand the old ceremony for the important donors

outcome.text: You lose public reputation and {{other}}’s trust by making the meal wait for precedence again.

events.title: THE FAVOUR WITH BOTH HANDS FREE
events.text: {{other}} remembers the promise you made while the wound was dressed. A practical household chore now needs the help you said you would give.

choices.label: Give the promised afternoon

outcome.text: You spend a little strength and deepen a real friendship. The favour is repaid through work, without claiming the wound never happened.

choices.label: Say the promise belonged to a frightening day

outcome.text: You lose trust with {{other}}. The knot has come untied more easily than the memory.

events.title: THE PEG KEPT ON THE BENCH
events.text: {{other}} has kept the peg you fitted before climbing the scaffold. Another worker asks why the smallest part of the job is being shown so proudly.

choices.label: Explain the repair without making the blessing a joke

outcome.text: You gain craft experience and trust. {{other}} is able to repeat the lesson without defending the earlier mistake.

choices.label: Make the explanation mostly about your own good sense

outcome.text: You gain charm and lose a little affection. The peg is patient enough to remain the useful part of the story.

events.title: THE GUARANTEE’S NEW WORDING
events.text: {{other}} returns with a tonic guarantee rewritten after your public objection. This version promises only that the bottle contains tonic.

choices.label: Welcome the smaller, honest promise

outcome.text: You improve trust and gain a little public standing. {{other}} has discovered a claim that fits inside the bottle.

choices.label: Keep clear of the seller without renewing the argument

outcome.text: You preserve your judgement and lose no money. {{other}} accepts that changed wording need not buy a customer.

events.title: THE INHERITANCE’S SECOND MESSENGER
events.text: {{other}} brings a new demand connected with the fortune you borrowed to pursue. The estate is still unnamed; its expenses have become very well documented.

choices.label: Refuse to finance the claim further

outcome.text: You gain judgement and lose {{other}}’s favour. The existing loans remain, but no new obligation is invented on their behalf.

choices.label: Put the demands before the clerk

outcome.text: You gain public standing and make {{other}} a rival. The supposed fortune has finally produced an identifiable person for the inquiry.

events.title: THE DEVIL REMEMBERS A FAIR WAGE
events.text: {{other}} remembers that you helped pay the pageant performer. A later neighbourhood task needs someone trusted to account for everyone’s work.

choices.label: Help keep the accounts fairly

outcome.text: You gain experience and public standing through a reputation based on an actual payment. {{other}} trusts you with the list.

choices.label: Decline the responsibility without insulting the work

outcome.text: You keep the evening free and preserve the acquaintance. The earlier kindness remains completed rather than becoming permanent employment.

events.title: THE STONE WHERE YOU PUT IT
events.text: {{other}} wants your help identifying a boundary mark. The stone restored before witnesses is still there, inconveniently available for everybody to inspect.

choices.label: Stand by the witnessed position

outcome.text: You improve family standing and trust. {{other}} is reminded that a useful agreement can survive without being rewritten.

choices.label: Keep out of the new argument

outcome.text: You preserve your time and lose some trust. The stone remains a better witness than the people avoiding it.

events.title: THE THING YOU BOUGHT BACK
events.text: {{other}} returns a small keepsake to your hand after you saved the household goods. This one, the explanation goes, should not need rescuing twice.

choices.label: Keep it without turning the gift into a debt

outcome.text: You deepen the family bond. The object carries no new price. {{other}} waits until you understand that part.

choices.label: Remind the giver what the rescue cost

outcome.text: You damage trust by making the gift another entry in the debt account. The actual loans are unchanged.

events.title: THE MOST ALIVE CORPSE
events.text: A draft claim lists {{parent}} as dead and asks for your household’s goods. {{parent}} arrives to dispute it. {{other}}, who supports the claim, asks whether the alleged deceased has brought a witness.

choices.label: Put your very audible parent before the witnesses

outcome.text: {{parent}} reads the claim aloud, adding objections in the margins. Your household keeps its goods; {{other}} acquires a personal reason to dislike you.

choices.label: Pay to withdraw the claim (9g)

outcome.text: You pay nine gold to stop a living person being inventoried. {{parent}} refuses to call the payment a funeral expense.

choices.label: Support the false claim and take the offered share (fraud)

outcome.text: {{other}} pays your share. {{parent}} supplies the court with a living witness against you: {{parent}}.

events.title: THE FUNERAL REHEARSAL
events.text: {{parent}} wants to hear the funeral speech while corrections are still possible. The first objection is to the word “patient.”

choices.label: Read the truthful version

outcome.text: {{parent}} disputes three dates and concedes one unkindness. You leave with a better account of the living person.

choices.label: Offer a magnificently flattering version

outcome.text: {{parent}} approves, then asks which parent you were describing. Affection survives the accusation.

events.title: THE INHERITANCE OF THREE KEYS
events.text: {{other}} offers to sell you three keys said to open a rich relative’s chest. The relative is less clearly identified than the price.

choices.label: Have a smith inspect them (3g)

outcome.text: The smith identifies a stable key, a padlock key and an ambitious piece of wire. You pay for the inspection and keep your savings.

choices.label: Buy the supposed inheritance (14g)

outcome.text: The keys open nothing you own. Fourteen gold has passed into a household with better working locks.

choices.label: Leave the chest to its remarkable relatives

outcome.text: You decline. {{other}} lowers the price so quickly that you feel richer without buying anything.

events.title: THE HOUSEHOLD’S NEW BAILIFF
events.text: {{child}} has begun charging visitors a toll of buttons. A visiting neighbour has paid in order to find out what happens next.

choices.label: Make the little collector restore every button

outcome.text: {{child}} returns the buttons under supervision. The household loses an afternoon and gains an accountant who now understands refunds.

choices.label: Declare the doorstep a lawful little manor

outcome.text: You defend the toll. The household’s standing falls, but {{child}} gains confidence in the hereditary nature of nonsense.

choices.label: Turn the whole levy into a counting lesson

outcome.text: You replace the toll with a game that gives the buttons back. {{child}} discovers that rules can be improved without conquering the neighbours.

events.title: THE BED IN THE WILL
events.text: {{sibling}} wants the better bed when your household divides its goods. The argument has reached the point of measuring old childhood injuries against the mattress.

choices.label: Trade the bed for a fair division of other goods

outcome.text: You surrender the bed and keep the dispute from becoming a family occupation. {{sibling}} thanks you without listing the injuries again.

choices.label: Offer to saw the bed exactly in half

outcome.text: {{sibling}} refuses the proposal and the relationship deteriorates. You keep the goods, together with the saw’s excellent negotiating reputation.

choices.label: Keep the goods together until there is actual need

outcome.text: The division waits. You use the intervening quiet to mend the bedding. It becomes easier to sleep on than the argument.

events.title: THE HEIR WITH THE WRONG FACE
events.text: {{parent}} commissions a little family portrait and asks that you be painted looking more like a prosperous relation. The painter has brought a ruler.

choices.label: Keep your own inconvenient face

outcome.text: The portrait remains unpainted while you explain yourself. {{parent}} is disappointed, but no commission fee leaves the household.

choices.label: Pay for an honest portrait instead (8g)

outcome.text: The painter uses your actual nose. {{parent}} admits the nose belongs to the household. You accept the nearest available thing to praise.

events.title: THE PENSION PAID IN BREAD
events.text: {{parent}} insists that support should arrive as bread rather than promises. The loaf specified in the agreement is drawn at its desired size.

choices.label: Set aside stores for the support

outcome.text: You put food into the household reserve and reduce the ready coin available to you. {{parent}} approves the part that can be sliced.

choices.label: Offer another elegantly worded promise

outcome.text: {{parent}} asks whether the promise can be toasted. Trust declines, though the question improves the discussion.

choices.label: Repair the hearth instead of pledging money

outcome.text: The household’s living conditions improve. {{parent}} accepts work that can be felt through a cold evening.

events.title: YOUR NAME UNDER SOMEONE ELSE’S DEBT
events.text: {{sibling}} has promised a lender that you will guarantee a loan. Your signature looks splendid, particularly for something you did not write.

choices.label: Buy back the false guarantee (18g)

outcome.text: You pay to retire the claim before it spreads. {{sibling}} is relieved; your trust in that relief is sharply reduced.

choices.label: Reject the forgery publicly

outcome.text: The family’s reputation suffers under the accusation. You keep your purse and acquire a genuine sibling rivalry in place of a counterfeit signature.

choices.label: Accept the obligation, not the forgery

negative: A debt remains to be repaid

outcome.text: You record a real twenty-gold debt in your own name. {{sibling}} promises to remember it; the lender has a more dependable method.

events.title: THE COAT WITH ROOM TO GROW
events.text: {{child}} hates the new coat because it has room for another child inside. The tailor calls this economy; {{child}} calls it a tent.

choices.label: Pay for a coat that fits this year (4g)

outcome.text: The sleeves stop collecting soup. {{child}} is delighted by the expensive discovery of wrists.

choices.label: Teach a fold that makes the sleeves useful

outcome.text: You fold, stitch and let {{child}} choose the thread. The household gains a small practical skill and a less furious wearer.

events.title: THE LADDER THAT IS NEVER HOME
events.text: {{other}} has borrowed your household’s ladder so often that visitors now ask directions to it rather than to you.

choices.label: Retrieve it and help finish the repair

outcome.text: You bring the ladder home after helping with the roof. {{other}} owes you a kindness, and the household can reach its own rafters again.

choices.label: Charge for this year’s use (5g)

outcome.text: {{other}} pays five gold and becomes much less neighbourly. The ladder has earned more than most apprentices.

choices.label: Give it away and make a lower set of shelves

outcome.text: You lose some household wealth but gain a grateful neighbour. The lower shelves produce fewer requests for help.

events.title: THE SALT CELLAR’S SECOND BOTTOM
events.text: {{parent}} shows you the household’s hidden savings beneath the salt. The ceremony would feel grander if the emergency reserve did not smell of herring.

choices.label: Leave the reserve where it is

outcome.text: You promise discretion. {{parent}} trusts you with something more substantial than a story.

choices.label: Take twelve gold from the household reserve

outcome.text: The household loses twelve gold and you gain it. {{parent}} discovers the missing weight before the missing salt.

choices.label: Add to the household reserve (6g)

outcome.text: The reserve grows. {{parent}} moves you from the category of people protected by it to the category of people protecting it.

events.title: THE CONDITIONAL BLESSING
events.text: {{child}} has written a promise to obey you “where reasonably convenient.” It has been copied beautifully.

choices.label: Discuss what convenient actually means

outcome.text: You agree on chores and limits. {{child}} keeps the phrase in the copy, now accompanied by a rather demanding definition.

choices.label: Tear up the qualifying words

outcome.text: You enforce obedience and damage trust. {{child}} learns to leave a wider margin for thoughts you will not read.

events.title: THE ROOF’S CONTRIBUTION TO SUPPER
events.text: Rain falls onto your household’s table. {{other}} offers a hurried roof repair, priced on the assumption that you have already noticed the weather.

choices.label: Pay for proper work (12g)

outcome.text: You pay for the roof repair. The household’s shelter improves and supper no longer requires moving the bowls between drops.

choices.label: Patch it together and lose a day’s rest

outcome.text: The patch improves the roof modestly. Your back protests a job that the clouds had made urgent.

choices.label: Spend nothing and let the room deteriorate

outcome.text: You preserve your purse while damp consumes part of the household’s food and furnishings. The economy is mostly imaginary.

events.title: THE STOLEN FAMILY ANECDOTE
events.text: {{sibling}} tells your most embarrassing childhood story and gives themselves your heroic part. You are left with the bucket.

choices.label: Restore the bucket’s true owner

outcome.text: You correct the story in front of everyone. {{sibling}} loses affection for you; your family’s standing survives its inability to agree about a bucket.

choices.label: Tell the part where both of you fell in

outcome.text: You trade a little dignity for a better laugh. {{sibling}} remembers why the original story was worth keeping.

events.title: THE HONEST LITTLE WITNESS
events.text: {{child}} saw you conceal goods during an argument over a levy. The child is now asking whether lying becomes lawful at a particular age.

choices.label: Return the goods and admit the example was poor

outcome.text: You pay restitution and restore your child’s trust. The explanation is harder than the payment.

choices.label: Teach silence by threatening punishment

outcome.text: {{child}} stops asking and loses trust in you. A household secret is created, together with a witness who has reasons to resent it.

choices.label: Challenge the assessment openly instead

outcome.text: You abandon concealment and put your objection in public. Your family’s reputation improves without settling the assessment for the court.

events.title: THE LAST HILL ON THE ROAD
events.text: {{parent}} insists the road is no steeper than it used to be. Only the pauses have grown longer.

choices.label: Take the road at your parent’s pace

outcome.text: You lose the afternoon and keep the company. {{parent}} lets you carry the basket without calling it help.

choices.label: Hire a cart for the journey (5g)

outcome.text: {{parent}} complains about the expense all the way home. The complaint is delivered from a comfortable seat.

choices.label: Leave the basket and hurry ahead

outcome.text: You preserve your time and damage your parent’s trust. The rest of the road is quieter than you expected.

events.title: THE HEIRLOOMS ON THE MARKET CLOTH
events.text: {{sibling}} is selling household keepsakes to meet a creditor. Each object comes with a family story. The buyers ask for shorter stories and lower prices.

choices.label: Buy the goods back for the household (20g)

outcome.text: You pay for the keepsakes and put them back in the household. {{sibling}} thanks you for saving the objects without making a speech over each one.

choices.label: Help make a fair sale

outcome.text: You accept that survival can require parting with things. The family’s standing improves and {{sibling}} trusts you more.

choices.label: Buy cheaply and keep the proceeds yourself

outcome.text: You profit from the sale while the household loses wealth. {{sibling}} recognises exactly which family tradition you have preserved.

events.title: THE FAMILY SEAL CUT IN SOAP
events.text: {{sibling}} has cut a convincing family seal in soap. It is clever, cheap and already on an agreement nobody authorised.

choices.label: Destroy the seal and pay to correct the agreement (10g)

outcome.text: The false seal dissolves in a basin. Ten gold pays for correction, and {{sibling}} discovers an expensive use for clean hands.

choices.label: Use the false seal to obtain an advance

outcome.text: You receive the advance and create a genuine forgery charge. The soap has left a wonderfully clear impression on the evidence.

charge.offence: Obtaining an advance with a false seal

choices.label: Give the impression to the clerk

outcome.text: You expose the scheme and damage your bond with {{sibling}}. The household’s reputation suffers, but your own legal record remains clear.

events.title: THE BOWL KEPT WARM
events.text: {{child}} has kept a bowl beside the hearth for you. It is nearly cold; the child has been watching it for a long time.

choices.label: Sit down and eat together

outcome.text: You eat slowly enough to hear the whole account of the day. {{child}} stops watching the bowl.

choices.label: Thank the child while attending to other work

outcome.text: Your thanks is sincere and your attention is elsewhere. {{child}} learns the difference.

events.title: THE BOUNDARY MARK UNDER THE BED
events.text: {{sibling}} has brought a boundary stone indoors for safekeeping. Unfortunately it was keeping two households from arguing about the field.

choices.label: Put it back before witnesses

outcome.text: The boundary is restored under witnesses rather than by memory. {{sibling}} helps carry it and resents the audience.

choices.label: Use the confusion to enlarge your household’s claim

outcome.text: Your household gains wealth from the disputed use, and you acquire a fraud charge. The stone is silent; the witnesses are not.

choices.label: Pay for a fresh survey (7g)

outcome.text: You fund a new survey and improve the household’s standing. {{sibling}} is disappointed that measuring settles what shouting could not.

events.title: THE WEDDING OF THREE GROOMS
events.text: {{sibling}} has promised to pay three different wedding brokers for one match. All three bring contracts to the same supper. The prospective marriage is the only part nobody has arranged.

choices.label: Read all three contracts aloud

outcome.text: You expose the conflicting promises. Family standing suffers and {{sibling}} blames the only person at supper who could read.

choices.label: Pay the brokers to cancel the claims (15g)

outcome.text: The contracts are cancelled for fifteen gold. Everybody leaves unmarried. The family counts this as the evening’s first clear success.

choices.label: Demand a share of the household’s wedding reserve

outcome.text: You take ten gold from the reserve. {{sibling}} now has three brokers and one blackmailer to satisfy.

events.title: THE INVENTORY OF MATRIMONY
events.text: {{spouse}} has drawn up a list of everything each of you brought to the marriage. Under your name, “confidence” is underlined twice.

choices.label: Add a fair account of the unpaid work

outcome.text: You list the work both of you do. {{spouse}} puts the inventory away before it needs another sheet.

choices.label: Prove that you brought more

outcome.text: You win the valuation and lose affection. {{spouse}} asks whether you would like a receipt for the triumph.

choices.label: Seek a formal separation and divide your goods

outcome.text: You end the marriage and surrender part of the household reserve. The list becomes useful in a way neither of you intended.

events.title: THE BENCH BETWEEN TWO FAMILIES
events.text: At your wedding anniversary meal, {{spouse}} objects to the order of the benches. Everyone insists that seating means nothing while refusing to move.

choices.label: Mix the benches and serve the food yourself

outcome.text: You put conversation before precedence. {{spouse}} helps, and the household’s reputation improves without buying another bench.

choices.label: Let your spouse choose the seats

outcome.text: {{spouse}} gets the arrangement right to at least one person’s satisfaction. Your willingness to yield is remembered kindly at home.

events.title: THE LOVE LETTER WITH A TALLY
events.text: {{other}} sends a declaration of affection on the back of a household account. The account is paid. This is the most encouraging part of the letter.

choices.label: Answer honestly, without promising a wedding

outcome.text: You begin a warmer acquaintance with {{other}}. Nobody is married by correspondence, though both of you enjoy the ink.

choices.label: Accept the offered marriage

outcome.text: You and {{other}} marry by mutual consent. The household account becomes the least interesting part of the document.

choices.label: Return a kind refusal

outcome.text: You decline without circulating the letter. {{other}} appreciates having one disappointment instead of an audience.

events.title: THE PETITION AGAINST YOUR EVENINGS
events.text: {{spouse}} asks why every errand takes you past the same doorway. You offer a well-prepared explanation. {{spouse}} asks how long you have been preparing it.

choices.label: Give a full account and change the arrangement

outcome.text: You answer the question and make room for your spouse’s worry. Trust improves through a less entertaining use of the evening.

choices.label: Turn the suspicion into a public joke

outcome.text: The joke reaches an audience. {{spouse}} withdraws affection and acquires a grievance that is entirely about what you actually did.

choices.label: End the marriage rather than answer

outcome.text: You choose separation. The marriage ends, the household loses resources and the unanswered question survives without a husband or wife to ask it.

events.title: A SUITOR’S EARLY TESTAMENT
events.text: {{other}} offers you a marriage contract and a draft will in the same sitting. The second document has been written considerably more neatly.

choices.label: Discuss how to live together before discussing death

outcome.text: You leave the contracts unsigned and the acquaintance more honest. {{other}} is relieved to put away the better pen.

choices.label: Accept the marriage without the speculative will

outcome.text: You marry {{other}} by consent. Neither of you gains an inheritance in advance of anyone’s death.

choices.label: Forge a richer settlement than you own

outcome.text: You create a false marriage settlement without making a marriage. {{other}} becomes a witness to the fraud, not your spouse.

events.title: THE GIFT RETURNED IN BETTER WRAPPING
events.text: {{other}} returns a courtship gift wrapped more beautifully than when it left you. The rejection appears to have received professional help.

choices.label: Accept the answer and admire the wrapping

outcome.text: You take the refusal without turning it into a quarrel. {{other}} trusts you more for the boundary you respect.

choices.label: Demand payment for the humiliation

outcome.text: You make an enemy of someone who had merely declined you. The wrapping is now the kindest part of the exchange.

events.title: A WITNESS TO THE WRONG ROMANCE
events.text: {{other}} asks you to swear you saw a courting couple promise marriage. You saw two people quarrel over a borrowed cloak, but the fee for remembering otherwise is tempting.

choices.label: Describe exactly what you saw

outcome.text: You refuse the false testimony. {{other}} loses trust in your usefulness; your own legal record remains untouched.

choices.label: Sign the false testimony for a promised reward

outcome.text: You accept a promise of payment and acquire a real perjury charge. The promised money is still only a promise.

choices.label: Warn the people whose names are being used

outcome.text: You publicly challenge the scheme. Your reputation rises while {{other}} acquires a specific grievance against you.

events.title: THE PRACTICAL LOVE POEM
events.text: {{spouse}} discovers a poem you wrote early in the marriage. Your present skill at remembering where the firewood is stored compares poorly with your former devotion.

choices.label: Fetch the wood before discussing the poem

outcome.text: The room warms and {{spouse}} accepts the new verse as an improvement. It has fewer adjectives and better fuel.

choices.label: Recite it with undiminished confidence

outcome.text: You make {{spouse}} laugh, though the wood remains where it was. Affection improves more than the room temperature.

events.title: THE IDENTICAL TOKEN
events.text: {{spouse}} finds a love token that looks exactly like one given to a neighbour. The pedlar who sold them is wisely absent.

choices.label: Admit the token came from a crowded stall

outcome.text: You admit that the token was common and the affection was not. {{spouse}} accepts the distinction after enjoying your discomfort.

choices.label: Commission something personal (7g)

outcome.text: Seven gold buys a token with a private inscription. {{spouse}} reads it twice before deciding not to ask what the first one cost.

choices.label: Accuse your spouse of inventing the comparison

outcome.text: You answer a small doubt with a larger cruelty. Trust falls, and the cheap token has become an expensive object.

events.title: THE PRICE OF PARTING
events.text: You and {{spouse}} are considering separation. The clerk has quoted for three copies: one for each of you and one for everyone who will pretend not to have read it.

choices.label: Pay for a formal separation (12g)

outcome.text: The marriage ends and twelve gold pays for the record. The clerk is the only person who calls the day satisfactory.

choices.label: Try an honest conversation before signing

outcome.text: You keep the marriage and rebuild a little trust. It is a beginning, not a miraculous repair.

choices.label: Destroy the draft and forbid further discussion

outcome.text: The marriage continues under less trust. A torn document is easier to silence than the person who asked for it.

events.title: THE DOWRY WHICH HONKS
events.text: {{spouse}} wants the household’s wedding reserve spent on food rather than another display of respectability. The proposed display has a ribbon budget larger than its supper budget.

choices.label: Put the money into household food (9g)

outcome.text: You fund the reserve and cancel the ribbons. {{spouse}} values an anniversary that can be eaten.

choices.label: Buy the display and leave supper thin (9g)

outcome.text: The ribbons are splendid and the household’s food reserve shrinks. {{spouse}} declines to be nourished by colour.

choices.label: Hold a quiet meal with what you have

outcome.text: You choose an unshowy supper and keep your savings. {{spouse}} enjoys not having to praise anything you have bought.

events.title: THE CHAPERONE’S EXPENSES
events.text: {{other}} brings an itemised account for supervising two people’s courtship. “Looking away at suitable moments” is the largest charge.

choices.label: Ask the supervised couple to review the account

outcome.text: You expose the exaggerated bill without inventing a romantic scandal. {{other}} dislikes the new interest in arithmetic.

choices.label: Pay to spare the couple an argument (5g)

outcome.text: You pay for discretion and dubious eyesight. {{other}} is pleased to find affection has a solvent friend.

events.title: THE SERENADE AT THE STOREROOM
events.text: {{other}} has been singing beneath a shutter that opens onto a storeroom. The household wants the flour left out of the next verse.

choices.label: Privately explain the mistake

outcome.text: You save {{other}} from a second performance and gain a grateful acquaintance. The flour remains unmoved.

choices.label: Call loudly for an encore

outcome.text: {{other}} discovers the error in public. Your reputation for wit rises slightly; your reputation with the singer falls considerably.

choices.label: Offer the singer a quiet cup indoors (3g)

outcome.text: You pay for a little hospitality and the humiliation passes without an audience. {{other}} remembers the door that actually opened.

events.title: THE GUEST WHO CAME WITH THE MARRIAGE
events.text: {{spouse}} has invited a relation to stay. “A short visit” has now acquired a spare blanket and an opinion about the way you cook.

choices.label: Agree on a leaving date together

outcome.text: You and {{spouse}} settle the invitation without a public quarrel. Household trust improves and the spare blanket remains only a blanket.

choices.label: Fund another week’s food (9g)

outcome.text: You pay for the visit and improve the food reserve. {{spouse}} appreciates generosity that does not arrive attached to a complaint.

choices.label: Order the guest out and blame your spouse

outcome.text: The household loses harmony and {{spouse}} loses trust in you. Winning the doorway has cost you something farther inside.

events.title: THE MATCHMAKER’S UNHELPFUL RECOMMENDATION
events.text: {{other}} recommends you for a marriage by praising your ability to withstand disappointment. You would prefer the compliment not to need so many examples.

choices.label: Set out what you actually want in a match

outcome.text: You replace a flattering description with an honest one. {{other}} understands you better and has less material for the next introduction.

choices.label: Invent impressive relations and property

outcome.text: Your invented position becomes a concealed falsehood. {{other}} is impressed by facts that will be expensive to defend.

events.title: THE ANNIVERSARY NEITHER MENTIONED
events.text: You and {{spouse}} have both forgotten the date of your marriage. Each of you is carefully waiting to see whether the other has remembered.

choices.label: Admit it first and share the relief

outcome.text: {{spouse}} laughs with the relief of a person acquitted before accusation. You begin a better evening than either of you had planned.

choices.label: Wait, then accuse your spouse of forgetting

outcome.text: You win a small advantage and spend it immediately on an argument. {{spouse}} is less inclined to celebrate the next year.

events.title: THE OATH THAT WAS NOT YOURS
events.text: {{other}} has circulated a claim that you promised marriage. You remember promising to return a borrowed pot. The pot is still at home.

choices.label: Return the pot before witnesses

outcome.text: You return the object you actually promised and reject the other claim publicly. {{other}} resents the clarity.

choices.label: Pay to withdraw the accusation (9g)

outcome.text: Nine gold buys an end to this claim, together with a secret about how readily your name can be priced.

choices.label: Produce a forged counterclaim

outcome.text: Your counterclaim reaches the clerk, who recognises the false seal. You face a forgery charge; the pot has become the most innocent participant.

charge.offence: Forging evidence in a marriage dispute

events.title: THE LORD WHO TAXED SHADE
events.text: {{other}} demands rent because your roof casts a shadow over a boundary. A servant has measured the offence at noon, when it is cheapest.

choices.label: Pay the demand (7g)

outcome.text: You pay seven gold for sunlight you were not using. {{other}} accepts the money without conceding the existence of clouds.

choices.label: Ask for a hearing with the measuring stick present

outcome.text: You bring the demand into public view. Your reputation rises and {{other}} becomes a named rival rather than an invisible expense.

choices.label: Help neighbouring households object together

outcome.text: The Commons gain confidence and {{other}}’s household records a feud with yours. Shade has become a matter of family honour.

familyFeud.reason: Opposed the demand for shadow rent

choices.label: Pay to mislay the measurements (4g)

outcome.text: Four gold makes the measurements difficult to find. A secret remains about the smaller, more useful payment.

events.title: THE WINDOW WITH A FEE
events.text: In your cell, daylight comes through a gap {{other}} says can be widened. The price is clear. The size of the wall beyond it is less so.

choices.label: Keep your money and mend the bedding

outcome.text: You remain imprisoned and make the cell marginally less miserable. {{other}} loses interest in your purse.

choices.label: Attempt the escape (risk a severe head injury)

success.text: You squeeze through and reach open ground. You are outside the prison, with an outstanding charge and very little dignity.

failure.text: The opening leads to a fall. You remain imprisoned with a head injury, and the wall proves much firmer than the offer.

choices.label: Tell the gaoler about the proposed opening

outcome.text: You remain inside, but your cooperation improves your reputation. {{other}} will not offer you another window.

events.title: THE PARDON WITH ROOM FOR A NAME
events.text: {{other}} offers a blank royal pardon, complete with a convincing stain where the seal ought to be. It forgives anything you are prepared to write small enough.

choices.label: Refuse the portable mercy

outcome.text: You decline the forgery. {{other}} moves on to people who have more to forgive and less to lose.

choices.label: Present it as genuine evidence

outcome.text: You acquire a fresh forgery charge without erasing any older one. The stain receives considerably more official attention than expected.

choices.label: Give the blank to the clerk as evidence

outcome.text: You expose the scheme and gain standing with the Crown. {{other}} knows exactly who supplied the paper.

events.title: THE THIEF WHO STOLE THE SIGN
events.text: {{other}} has stolen a tradesperson’s sign rather than any goods. Customers are now queuing outside the thief’s empty shed.

choices.label: Help return the sign before opening time

outcome.text: You restore the sign and gain local standing. {{other}} calls this a waste of an unusually successful theft.

choices.label: Sell directions to the wrong shop (risk a fraud complaint)

success.text: You collect a small payment before the joke is discovered. The shed remains empty and you keep a secret about the route you sold.

failure.text: A customer follows the directions with you still in sight. The complaint names both the empty shed and the person selling its address.

charge.offence: Taking payment for a false shop

events.title: THE JUROR’S LUNCH
events.text: {{other}} asks you to carry a handsome pie to a juror. Inside the lid is the verdict the sender would prefer him to reach.

choices.label: Deliver the whole thing as evidence

outcome.text: You expose the attempted bribe and gain public standing. {{other}} regards the crust as a betrayal.

choices.label: Carry the suggested verdict discreetly

outcome.text: The delivery makes you a party to attempted bribery. The pie is consumed; the written suggestion is kept.

charge.offence: Carrying a bribe to a juror

choices.label: Return it unopened to its owner

outcome.text: You decline the errand and lose a little favour with {{other}}. Your supper remains your own responsibility.

events.title: THE PAID SUBSTITUTE
events.text: {{other}} offers a purse if you will stand in for a relative’s punishment. The promised mark on your arm is described as small by someone who will not be wearing it.

choices.label: Refuse a punishment that is not yours

outcome.text: You keep your arm unmarked and disappoint {{other}}. It is an exceptionally affordable disappointment.

choices.label: Accept the money and the lasting injury

outcome.text: You receive twenty-four gold and a painful burn that leaves chronic pain. {{other}} is satisfied that the family punishment has been properly outsourced.

choices.label: Expose the proposed substitution

outcome.text: The public accusation damages {{other}}’s trust in you and improves your own standing. No part of the payment reaches your skin.

events.title: THE CLEANEST EVIDENCE
events.text: {{other}} wants a disputed receipt washed until the inconvenient line vanishes. The laundress has asked whether justice should be boiled with the linens.

choices.label: Keep the receipt dry and legible

outcome.text: You preserve the evidence and anger {{other}}. Your reputation improves for resisting a surprisingly domestic form of fraud.

choices.label: Wash away the line (risk an evidence charge)

success.text: The line vanishes before another copy can be compared. You keep the secret and gain {{other}}’s trust in your willingness to cross a boundary.

failure.text: A retained copy exposes the missing line. You acquire an evidence-destruction charge; the paper is cleaner than the account of washing it.

choices.label: Pay for witnessed copies before washing (3g)

outcome.text: You fund copies and make the original trick useless. {{other}} has to dispute what the document says instead of whether anyone can read it.

events.title: THE PRISON SUPPER LIST
events.text: Your cell’s meal list includes meat for four people. {{other}} asks whether anybody has seen either the meat or the other three.

choices.label: Add your name to a truthful complaint

outcome.text: You remain imprisoned and gain a little public standing for the complaint. {{other}} becomes a firmer ally inside the walls.

choices.label: Share a better prison meal (8g)

outcome.text: You buy food to share instead of waiting for the list to become edible. You recover some health and {{other}} trusts the meal more than the list.

choices.label: Save your own portion and refuse the argument

outcome.text: You preserve your strength at the cost of your cellmate’s affection. The list remains remarkably well fed.

events.title: THE ALIBI WITH A HOLE IN IT
events.text: {{other}} wants you to swear you spent the night together. The proposed alibi includes an hour when the whole square saw you somewhere else.

choices.label: Point out the missing hour

outcome.text: You refuse the story and retain a clear legal record. {{other}} resents the accuracy of your memory.

choices.label: Swear to the impossible evening (risk perjury)

success.text: The contradiction is not tested at this hearing. {{other}} gains trust in you and you acquire a secret whose witnesses still live in the square.

failure.text: The missing hour is put to witnesses. You acquire a perjury charge with unusually easy evidence.

events.title: THE ROPE INSPECTOR
events.text: {{other}} asks you to test a condemned climbing rope before it is sold again. The test consists of trusting the seller’s statement that it was only condemned on a technicality.

choices.label: Cut the rope so it cannot be sold

outcome.text: You destroy a dangerous bargain and gain public trust. {{other}} loses faith in your respect for private property.

choices.label: Test it above the quarry (risk a fatal fall)

success.text: The rope holds long enough for you to come down. You are paid ten gold and acquire an enduring dislike of technicalities.

failure.text: The condemned section parts over the quarry. The last assurance you hear is that it held yesterday.

effects.death: Killed in a fall while testing a condemned rope.

choices.label: Leave the seller without endorsing the rope

outcome.text: You decline to give an opinion that somebody might later mistake for a guarantee. {{other}} will need a different signature.

events.title: THE CHICKENS UNDER GUARD
events.text: {{other}} supports a new fine for wandering hens. The guard hired to watch the impounded birds is a dog, and expenses are rising whenever it looks hungry.

choices.label: Challenge the expense list publicly

outcome.text: You make the claim difficult to defend and gain standing with the Commons. {{other}} becomes a rival with a remarkably poultry-shaped grievance.

choices.label: Contribute to the households’ release fund (6g)

outcome.text: You contribute to the relief fund. Your family’s reputation improves; the dog remains the only participant without a receipt.

choices.label: Claim the release money with forged ownership papers

outcome.text: You obtain eleven gold and a fraud charge. Several actual owners are able to identify what you do not own.

charge.offence: Claiming impounded birds with false papers

events.title: THE KEY THAT OPENS EVERY DOOR
events.text: {{other}} claims to have a prison key that opens every door. It is drawn on parchment. The proposed escape requires a smith and a great deal of belief.

choices.label: Keep out of the scheme

outcome.text: You remain imprisoned without adding another charge to your record. {{other}} calls you unadventurous from inside a locked room.

choices.label: Commission the key and attempt escape (10g; more prison if caught)

success.text: The copied key opens a service door. You escape the cell, but remain wanted for breaking custody.

failure.text: The key turns in nothing. The search finds the drawing and adds three years to your sentence.

choices.label: Surrender the plan without accusing anyone else

outcome.text: You improve your public standing by surrendering the plan. {{other}} now regards you as a rival; your cell door is still locked.

events.title: THE WITNESS IN A DIFFERENT CAP
events.text: {{other}} offers to testify twice in a boundary dispute using a different cap for the second appearance. The caps are convincing. The beard is exactly the same.

choices.label: Stop the second testimony

outcome.text: You expose the trick and improve your standing. {{other}} cannot decide which cap to wear while resenting you.

choices.label: Act surprised at the second witness (risk a charge)

success.text: You sustain the performance long enough to escape immediate questioning. {{other}} trusts you more, and the deception remains a dangerous secret.

failure.text: The beard is recognised between the two caps. You acquire a false-testimony charge for pretending not to notice it.

events.title: THE THIEF’S CONFESSION BOOK
events.text: {{other}} has stolen the book in which a penitent listed stolen goods. It may be the only theft in the lane that comes with its own inventory.

choices.label: Return the book without reading it aloud

outcome.text: You protect the private confession and improve your reputation. {{other}} sees the book depart without any of the profit intended for it.

choices.label: Use the list to demand money

outcome.text: You create a blackmail charge and a secret about your own conduct. Confession has finally added something to the list.

choices.label: Hand it to the clerk as evidence of the theft

outcome.text: You expose the theft and anger {{other}}. The book is treated as evidence rather than as an invitation to collect from everyone in it.

events.title: THE FINE FOR BEING AVAILABLE
events.text: A clerk has put your name on an unpaid fine because you were standing nearest the desk. {{other}} offers to vouch for you, provided you explain what innocence usually pays.

choices.label: Request the original charge and witnesses

outcome.text: You contest the clerical shortcut and gain local standing. {{other}} is disappointed to discover that assistance can be made unnecessary.

choices.label: Pay five gold and keep your day (5g)

outcome.text: You pay the disputed amount without creating a criminal conviction. The receipt is more certain than the accusation ever was.

choices.label: Alter the account to name a neighbour

outcome.text: You create an actual forgery charge while trying to escape an administrative error. The clerk now has something definite to write.

events.title: THE COFFIN WHICH RATTLES
events.text: {{other}} offers work carrying a coffin that rattles like tableware. The supposed mourner asks you not to tilt his uncle.

choices.label: Ask to see the contents before agreeing

outcome.text: You refuse blind involvement in the smuggling. {{other}} withdraws the offer and a little of their goodwill.

choices.label: Carry it past the toll (risk a smuggling charge)

success.text: You carry the contraband through and earn thirteen gold. {{other}} is grateful that you mourned at a steady walking pace.

failure.text: A lid slips and the customs men discover the uncle’s astonishing collection of spoons. A smuggling charge is entered against you.

charge.offence: Carrying concealed goods past a toll

choices.label: Leave the uncle to his own household

outcome.text: You decline before taking the load. Whatever is in the coffin will have to find someone else to be late for it.

events.title: THE APOLOGY SOLD BY THE LINE
events.text: {{other}} offers to draft an apology for your past misdeeds. Every admission costs extra, and the most expensive one is true.

choices.label: Make a plain apology yourself

outcome.text: You take responsibility without buying eloquence. Public reputation improves a little and the existing charges remain for the court to decide.

choices.label: Buy a careful public statement (6g)

outcome.text: You pay for a statement worth reading aloud. Your reputation improves; the document does not pardon a single offence.

choices.label: Threaten the writer into silence

outcome.text: You add a threat to the conduct that needed an apology. {{other}} becomes a rival with a useful memory.

events.title: THE NAME THAT BUYS A CELL
events.text: {{other}} claims that naming an accomplice will improve your conditions. The requested name belongs to someone you have no evidence against.

choices.label: Refuse to invent an accomplice

outcome.text: You remain imprisoned and keep your own testimony honest. {{other}} loses interest in your memory.

choices.label: Give the unsupported accusation

outcome.text: You gain no automatic release. Instead, you add a false-testimony charge to the record and make {{other}} party to a dangerous confidence.

choices.label: Pay for a petition about your actual conditions (5g)

outcome.text: You pay for a truthful petition and gain public standing. The prison sentence continues while the complaint is considered.

events.title: THE LIE EVERYONE PRACTISED
events.text: {{other}} rehearses a witness’s story so thoroughly that you are asked to supply the correct pause before the false accusation.

choices.label: Refuse to become the rehearsal’s witness

outcome.text: You reject the falsehood and gain a reputation for independence. {{other}} loses trust in you as an accomplice.

choices.label: Give the rehearsed accusation under oath (prison)

outcome.text: The contradiction is exposed and you are imprisoned for perjury. The court finds your perfectly timed hesitation especially persuasive evidence.

choices.label: Expose the rehearsal before testimony begins

outcome.text: You expose the scheme and acquire a named rival. {{other}} will have to rehearse a different explanation.

events.title: THE CONSTABLE’S SINGLE BOOT
events.text: {{other}} has found a constable’s boot with a purse inside. The missing constable is calling the theft an assault on authority; the boot looks undamaged.

choices.label: Return the boot and its contents

outcome.text: You return the find and improve your reputation. Authority is restored to a matching pair.

choices.label: Keep the purse and leave the boot (risk a theft charge)

success.text: You keep the purse’s contents and leave the boot where it will be found. {{other}} knows enough to make the money less comfortable than it feels.

failure.text: The constable finds the emptied boot before you have left the lane. The resulting theft charge includes an unusually recognisable piece of evidence.

charge.offence: Keeping the contents of a constable’s stolen boot

events.title: THE BARREL WITH A SECOND FLOOR
events.text: {{other}} wants your mark on barrels that hold less than their stated measure. The false bottoms fit beautifully. Honesty is the only badly made part.

choices.label: Keep your mark off the barrels

outcome.text: Your standing in the guild improves when you refuse. {{other}} looks for a craftsman whose signature is more flexible than the wood.

choices.label: Sign them and accept the fraudulent commission

outcome.text: You earn sixteen gold and create a fraud charge. The barrels’ workmanship is much easier to defend than your mark.

choices.label: Rework them into honestly sized vessels

outcome.text: The extra labour hurts your performance this year but earns experience and public standing. You have finally made something smaller without cheating.

events.title: THE CUSTOMER’S ROYAL ELL
events.text: {{other}} measures your finished work with an “ancient royal ell” that gets longer at the expensive end of the job.

choices.label: Bring the guild’s measure before discussing payment

outcome.text: You defend the agreed measure and gain guild standing. {{other}} loses confidence in the profitability of ancient custom.

choices.label: Do the extra work to keep the peace

outcome.text: You absorb the extra labour and gain a more grateful customer. Your performance suffers under the time it takes.

events.title: THE LEFT-HANDED APPRENTICE
events.text: {{other}} says an apprentice’s work is wrong because the tool is held in the wrong hand. The joint fits perfectly. This is becoming an awkward fact.

choices.label: Judge the work by the joint

outcome.text: You defend useful skill and improve your standing. {{other}} is less pleased to discover that custom can be tested against a table.

choices.label: Insist on the customary hand

outcome.text: You enforce the rule, lose experience you might have gained and damage your reputation for fair judgement. The joint remains correct.

choices.label: Ask to be taught the method

outcome.text: You gain practical experience by risking the appearance of not already knowing everything. {{other}} watches you put down the rulebook.

events.title: THE MASTER’S MARK ON RUBBISH
events.text: {{other}} has found your mark on rejected goods. You can deny it, correct it or admit that someone has been selling what you were paid to discard.

choices.label: Recall the marked goods at your own expense (18g)

outcome.text: You fund the correction and preserve your post. Guild standing suffers less than your purse, and {{other}} accepts the repair.

choices.label: Deny the mark despite the matching die

outcome.text: The deception costs you your employment and a fraud charge is entered. The die continues to recognise its own work.

charge.offence: Selling rejected goods under a master’s mark

choices.label: Admit the breach and surrender the post

outcome.text: You leave the employment and lose guild standing. The admission avoids a new fabricated defence, not the consequences of the original breach.

events.title: THE DRY GOODS IN THE RIVER
events.text: {{other}} proposes a shipping venture described as dry goods. The proposed barge has no cover and the sky has supplied a rebuttal.

choices.label: Delay the venture and lose the small booking fee (3g)

outcome.text: You pay the booking fee and keep the capital out of the river. {{other}} dislikes your caution until it rains harder.

choices.label: Borrow to fund the shipment (risk debt and household loss)

success.text: The goods arrive before the storm. The return reaches your purse, while the full loan remains a real debt to repay.

failure.text: The shipment fails. Your thirty-gold loan survives it, and the household loses wealth meeting the immediate costs.

choices.label: Pay for cover before committing a small stake (9g)

outcome.text: You pay for better protection and gain trading experience without inventing a guaranteed profit. {{other}} trusts your terms more than the forecast.

events.title: THE SILENT PARTNER’S SPEECH
events.text: {{other}} proposes a silent partnership and spends an hour explaining how loudly you should defend it to creditors.

choices.label: Demand written limits to your liability

outcome.text: You improve your working judgement and lose a little of {{other}}’s enthusiasm. Silence turns out to have conditions.

choices.label: Guarantee the debt to secure the partnership

negative: A debt remains to be repaid

outcome.text: You record a twenty-two-gold obligation and gain a more trusting partner. Trust is cheap to offer when the other person signs.

choices.label: Keep trading on your own account

outcome.text: You decline the partnership and preserve your independent standing. {{other}} is left with the entire silence to finance.

events.title: THE SCALE THAT WEIGHS HONOUR
events.text: {{other}} challenges your measures by putting an empty purse on the scales and declaring your honesty too light.

choices.label: Invite three ordinary customers to test the measure

outcome.text: You demonstrate the measure and gain guild standing. {{other}} discovers that an audience can have a use besides laughing.

choices.label: Answer the insult with a better one

outcome.text: You win attention and gain a workplace rival. Your performance slips while you keep supplying new material.

events.title: THE WOOL WHICH MOVES BY ITSELF
events.text: {{other}} offers a cheap consignment of wool. A sleeve emerges from the sack before its owner, and several moths emerge before either.

choices.label: Reject the stock before paying

outcome.text: You refuse damaged goods and gain experience. {{other}} says you are missing an opportunity; the moths are already taking theirs.

choices.label: Buy a small lot for honest salvage (5g)

outcome.text: You pay for the damaged lot and gain craft experience sorting what can be used. No miraculous resale profit arrives with it.

choices.label: Sell it on without disclosing the damage

outcome.text: You earn nine gold and gain a fraud complaint. The moths prove more candid witnesses than your description.

events.title: THE EEL IN THE RENT ROLL
events.text: {{other}} reads a customary rent that includes one eel per strip. The stream has been dry for two summers. Tradition, the explanation goes, is not responsible for water.

choices.label: Petition for a money equivalent based on actual prices

outcome.text: You gain standing with neighbouring households and experience managing rents. {{other}} resents being asked to price the impossible.

choices.label: Pay five gold to settle this year’s demand

outcome.text: You settle the demand in coin. {{other}} accepts a form of eel that is much easier to keep in a purse.

events.title: THE PLOUGH’S DAY OF REST
events.text: {{other}} insists that a damaged plough must rest on a saint’s day. The plough has been resting all week; the field is less devout.

choices.label: Repair the plough before the next working day

outcome.text: You spend your rest on the repair and gain husbandry experience. The field’s prospects improve without altering the calendar.

choices.label: Observe the day and accept the lost work

outcome.text: You gain faith and lose some work performance. {{other}} approves of a sacrifice you are both able to measure.

choices.label: Borrow sound equipment on a clear promise

negative: A debt remains to be repaid

outcome.text: You complete the work and gain a real six-gold obligation. The borrowed blade is sharper than the distinction between favour and debt.

events.title: THE HAYSTACK’S OWNER
events.text: {{other}} claims a haystack by counting how many people watched it being built. You counted the days you worked on it.

choices.label: Bring a clear account of the labour

outcome.text: You defend your work and gain public standing. {{other}} dislikes an account that cannot be enlarged by inviting friends.

choices.label: Accept a smaller share to avoid losing the whole season

outcome.text: You concede some household food and improve your working relationship. It is a peace with a visible price.

events.title: THE PRICE OF A MISSING NOT
events.text: {{other}} asks you to copy an agreement whose most expensive word is “not.” The draft fee increases if you happen to omit it.
