choices.label: Copy every inconvenient word correctly

outcome.text: You keep the text honest and improve your professional standing. {{other}} pays you in displeasure rather than praise.

choices.label: Take the dishonest fee and omit it

outcome.text: You gain twelve gold and a forgery charge. One missing word has found a remarkably large place in the evidence.

choices.label: Require both parties to approve the new wording

outcome.text: You force the proposed change into the open. Your reputation and experience rise; the secret fee disappears.

events.title: THE TWO ORIGINAL COPIES
events.text: {{other}} brings two “original” deeds that disagree about a field. Both carry the same date, ink and confident assertion of uniqueness.

choices.label: Compare witnesses before endorsing either

outcome.text: You gain experience from a slower, sounder inquiry. {{other}} must wait for a result that can survive being read twice.

choices.label: Endorse the more profitable copy without inquiry

outcome.text: You create a fraud charge and lose guild standing. The other original remains inconveniently original.

events.title: THE CERTIFICATE OF EXCELLENT HEALTH
events.text: {{other}} wants a certificate saying you found no illness. The requested wording includes a date on which you never examined anyone.

choices.label: Offer a real examination and an accurate report

outcome.text: You improve your professional performance by refusing to diagnose a date. {{other}} trusts your work more than your convenience.

choices.label: Backdate the certificate for payment

outcome.text: You receive seventeen gold and a fraud charge. Your employment is lost when the false certificate is challenged.

choices.label: Decline the certificate altogether

outcome.text: You keep your record clean and lose a little client affection. The unexamined patient remains unexamined, whatever the letter wanted.

events.title: THE CONSULTATION JAR
events.text: {{other}} brings a sealed jar for diagnosis and admits, after some questioning, that three households contributed to it to save the consultation fee.

choices.label: Explain why the samples must be separate

outcome.text: You gain experience and improve the client’s trust without inventing a diagnosis. The jar is now a problem of disposal rather than medicine.

choices.label: Give one confident diagnosis for everyone

outcome.text: Your performance and professional standing fall. The certainty is remembered; a genuine cure has not taken place.

events.title: THE PATRON’S IMPROVED LAST VERSE
events.text: {{other}} wants your performance to end with a direct accusation of treason against a powerful household. The patron describes the risk as literary.

choices.label: Refuse to turn a rhyme into testimony

outcome.text: You preserve your freedom and lose the patron’s favour. The unfinished rhyme is an unusually safe silence.

choices.label: Perform the accusation (risk prison and dismissal)

success.text: The hall treats the verse as satire and you earn nineteen gold. {{other}} applauds the boldness from a comfortable distance.

failure.text: The accusation is treated as a deliberate falsehood. You lose your employment and are imprisoned for the performance.

choices.label: Offer a verse about the patron’s own courage

outcome.text: You turn the proposed risk back toward its owner. Your reputation rises; {{other}} declines the opportunity to become the subject.

events.title: THE SONG PAID FOR BY THE PAUSE
events.text: {{other}} offers to pay you to stop between verses so a rival performer can be heard from the next yard. It is the first time your silence has received a proper offer.

choices.label: Share the interval openly

outcome.text: You make room for the second performance and gain a cooperative reputation. {{other}} appreciates having arranged something without a feud.

choices.label: Sing straight through the rival’s turn

outcome.text: You win attention and damage your professional standing. {{other}} now knows which agreements require a louder bell.

events.title: THE LETTER IN THE SAND BOX
events.text: {{other}} wants you to dry a confidential letter over sand that will preserve an impression of its contents. Curiosity has supplied its own copying method.

choices.label: Use fresh sand and destroy the impression

outcome.text: You protect the confidence and improve your performance. {{other}} dislikes the tidy disposal of an opportunity.

choices.label: Keep the impression for future leverage

outcome.text: You create a concealed record and a secret about your conduct. Your work gains experience in a direction a good patron would not recommend.

choices.label: Tell the sender what was proposed

outcome.text: You expose the trick, gain standing and acquire a workplace rival. {{other}} has learned something about the speed of letters.

events.title: THE BOOTS FOR THE LEFT FOOT
events.text: {{other}} brings a company supply order for boots. Every pair contains two left feet, which the contractor describes as excellent uniformity.

choices.label: Reject the issue before the company marches

outcome.text: You improve your performance and gain the company’s respect. {{other}} has to find a buyer with less demanding feet.

choices.label: Rework the issue with the company cobbler

outcome.text: You gain practical experience and lose some health to the long repair. The men can march, though no one praises the shape.

choices.label: Certify the issue and take the dishonest fee

outcome.text: You earn thirteen gold and create a supply-fraud charge. The evidence walks badly but reaches the clerk.

events.title: THE BAND’S HONEST ACCOUNTANT
events.text: {{other}} has drawn up an impeccably fair division of loot. Unfortunately the calculation includes goods nobody has stolen yet.

choices.label: Divide only what is actually available

outcome.text: You improve your working judgement and the band’s trust. Arithmetic proves useful even in an irregular profession.

choices.label: Promise your share of the imagined haul

negative: A debt remains to be repaid

outcome.text: You gain favour and record a real fourteen-gold obligation. The debt is the first item in the account to become entirely genuine.

choices.label: Take a larger share through a false count

outcome.text: You gain ten gold and acquire a feud with {{other}}. An outlaw’s account can be corrected without consulting a court.

familyFeud.reason: A false division of the band’s proceeds

events.title: THE ROYAL FEAST OF DISASTER
events.text: A visiting envoy’s falcon has been served at supper. {{other}} recognises its silver ring and offers to say it was a diplomatic gift if you will support the story. The cook offers the remaining wing.

choices.label: Admit the disaster and fund compensation (16g)

outcome.text: You pay for compensation and improve your family’s reputation for candour. {{other}} is relieved that the bird’s final journey need not become a border dispute.

choices.label: Blame your named dining companion

outcome.text: You accuse {{other}} and damage that relationship into a rivalry. Your own family gains an enemy household; the falcon gains no useful explanation.

familyFeud.reason: A false accusation over the envoy’s falcon

choices.label: Insist on an accurate account without promising funds

outcome.text: You preserve an honest account and gain Crown standing. {{other}} loses some affection for the witness who refused to improve the story.

events.title: THE PORTRAIT THAT EXPECTS A BOW
events.text: {{other}} wants visitors to bow to a newly painted likeness before seeing its owner. The portrait has the more forgiving expression.

choices.label: Bow to the painted rank and save your quarrel

outcome.text: You gain favour with {{other}} at a small cost to your own dignity. The portrait accepts the salute without keeping score.

choices.label: Address only the person who can answer

outcome.text: You preserve your reputation for independence and make a rival. {{other}} finds the portrait’s visitors much easier to manage.

choices.label: Praise the portrait’s restraint

outcome.text: The compliment reaches {{other}} a moment late. You gain charm and lose a little trust in the room.

events.title: THE CELLAR BELOW THE PRECEDENT
events.text: {{other}} claims your household must keep storing grain in a cellar that floods. The right to use it is ancient; the water is fresh.

choices.label: Pay to drain and repair the store (22g)

outcome.text: You pay for the work. Household shelter and food reserves improve, and {{other}} accepts a useful alteration to custom.

choices.label: Insist that inherited rights need no repair

outcome.text: You preserve your cash while the household loses stored food and wealth. The right to an empty cellar remains unimpaired.

choices.label: Move the argument into a public petition

outcome.text: You gain Commons standing and lose favour with {{other}}. The household’s current stores are not miraculously moved by the petition.

events.title: THE ANCESTOR WHO CHANGED SIDES
events.text: {{other}} offers to improve your pedigree by inserting a famous commander. Unfortunately the commander fought against the Crown your family currently serves.

choices.label: Keep the inconveniently ordinary pedigree

outcome.text: You retain an honest family account and improve Crown standing. {{other}} must sell the commander to a household with different loyalties.

choices.label: Adopt the impressive false pedigree

outcome.text: Your family enjoys a brief rise in standing and gains a concealed false lineage. The document can now be challenged as a forgery.

events.title: THE COUNCIL CHAIR AT AUCTION
events.text: {{other}} is selling the right to sit in a chair outside the council room. The wording is careful about which side of the door it is on.

choices.label: Read the grant aloud before the bidding

outcome.text: You expose the limited claim and gain Crown standing. {{other}} loses trust in your appreciation of furniture.

choices.label: Buy the public appearance of access (10g)

outcome.text: You pay ten gold for a conspicuous seat, not an office. Your family’s reputation rises slightly; the council seals stay with their holders.

choices.label: Remain standing and keep the money

outcome.text: You decline the chair. {{other}} cannot decide whether you are poor or unusually well informed.

events.title: THE AMBASSADOR’S BLANK PAGE
events.text: {{other}} asks you to witness a document before its terms are filled in. The argument for speed is that peace is too important to wait for words.

choices.label: Require the terms before witnessing

outcome.text: You gain standing for refusing a blank commitment. {{other}} must interrupt the urgency long enough to say what it is for.

choices.label: Witness the blank and hope for favourable terms

outcome.text: You become party to a fraudulent instrument and acquire a legal charge. Peace has been given an alarmingly broad margin.

charge.offence: Witnessing a knowingly blank diplomatic instrument

choices.label: Offer to copy complete terms under witnesses

outcome.text: You improve Crown standing and professional judgement without promising a treaty no one has written.

events.title: THE HUNT THAT STOPPED AT AN ALTAR
events.text: {{other}}’s hunting party has cornered a deer beside a wayside altar. Several people are arguing about sanctuary; the deer appears strongly in favour.

choices.label: Ask the party to leave the animal alone

outcome.text: You gain Church standing and lose hunting favour with {{other}}. The altar keeps the quieter congregation.

choices.label: Fund a meal instead of the disputed hunt (8g)

outcome.text: You pay for supper and lower local religious tension. {{other}} accepts a peace that comes with a table.

events.title: THE PRICE OF THE THIRD WHISPER
events.text: {{other}} offers you a secret whose first two buyers are standing across the hall. Both look disappointed to find the information still available.

choices.label: Refuse to become the third exclusive owner

outcome.text: You ask to meet the other exclusive owners. {{other}} withdraws the offer before exclusivity can become a public meeting.

choices.label: Pay for the rumour, knowing it may be worthless (5g)

outcome.text: You pay five gold for an unverified rumour. No actual secret is revealed merely because someone priced it as one.

choices.label: Tell the buyers they have been sold exclusivity together

outcome.text: You expose the sales trick and gain a named rival. {{other}} is forced to offer a less crowded form of discretion.

events.title: THE ARMOUR FOR A SMALLER ANCESTOR
events.text: {{other}} offers you ancestral armour for a ceremonial ride. The breastplate remembers a slimmer family.

choices.label: Pay to fit the armour safely (11g)

outcome.text: You pay for alteration rather than for endurance. {{other}} admires the result without admitting it needed work.

choices.label: Ride in the tight armour (risk a crushed fall)

success.text: You survive the ride and acquire a modest reputation for composure. Nobody sees how slowly you take your next breath.

failure.text: You fall badly when the armour prevents a safe dismount. A broken bone makes the family resemblance newly painful.

choices.label: Ride in your own ordinary clothes

outcome.text: You avoid the injury and lose some of {{other}}’s ceremonial favour. Your ancestors will have to be recognised by your face.

events.title: THE CHILD’S LARGE SIGNATURE
events.text: {{other}} asks you to endorse an order attributed to the young ruler. The handwriting is a fine adult hand, except where someone has added an ornamental blot.

choices.label: Request the regent’s public confirmation

outcome.text: You improve Crown standing by asking for lawful confirmation. {{other}} dislikes the number of adults now reading the order.

choices.label: Endorse the doubtful signature

outcome.text: You create a forgery charge and gain favour with {{other}}. The blot has not made the document any younger.

events.title: THE GUEST WHO COMES WITH A RANSOM
events.text: {{other}} wants you to keep a “guest” until a disputed ransom is paid. The guest has asked why hospitality requires a barred door.

choices.label: Refuse to make your household a private prison

outcome.text: You gain public standing and lose favour with {{other}}. Your doors remain useful for entering as well as leaving.

choices.label: Support the proposed unlawful detention

outcome.text: You acquire a charge for aiding unlawful detention. {{other}} calls you a dependable host. The description is entered among the evidence.

choices.label: Fund a witnessed negotiation (9g)

outcome.text: You pay to convene a negotiation and gain Crown standing. No ransom is declared settled until the parties actually agree.

events.title: THE MAP WITH AN OBEDIENT RIVER
events.text: {{other}} presents a map on which a boundary river bends conveniently around a disputed estate. The actual river has not been consulted.

choices.label: Insist on a new survey rather than a better drawing

outcome.text: You gain standing and anger {{other}} by distinguishing a claim from geography.

choices.label: Attest to the false boundary

outcome.text: You create a boundary-fraud charge. {{other}} gains confidence in you while the evidence acquires a riverbank.

charge.offence: Attesting a knowingly false boundary map

events.title: THE COLOURS OF YOUR ENEMY
events.text: {{other}} has ordered banners using your family’s colours in the order worn by a rival household. The herald says the difference is obvious once someone starts fighting.

choices.label: Pay to correct them before the procession (7g)

outcome.text: You pay for the correction and improve your household’s public standing. {{other}} thanks you for solving the argument before it needed a wound.

choices.label: Carry plain banners and explain the mistake

outcome.text: You avoid a false claim at a small cost to public dignity. The family’s reputation for honesty improves.

choices.label: Use the confusion to provoke the other household

outcome.text: You damage public order and create a lasting family feud with {{other}} over the deliberate provocation.

events.title: THE MUSTER OF THE ABSENT MEN
events.text: {{other}} submits a list of fighting men that includes a grandfather, a departed groom and one name written twice with different hats.

choices.label: Publish the actual strength

outcome.text: You improve Crown standing and offend {{other}}. The force becomes smaller on paper and no smaller in the field.

choices.label: Certify the full list for a fee

outcome.text: You earn fifteen gold and acquire a military fraud charge. No extra soldiers emerge from the new ink.

choices.label: Fund a modest recruitment effort (12g)

outcome.text: You spend twelve gold and slightly reduce war threat. {{other}} approves of a remedy paid for in someone else’s coin.

events.title: THE TOAST TO YOUR GOOD FORTUNE
events.text: {{other}} drinks to your future success while quietly suggesting it would be kinder if you found it elsewhere.

choices.label: Ask openly what your rival wants

outcome.text: You turn the insinuation into a clear disagreement. Public reputation improves while {{other}}’s affection falls.

choices.label: Offer a limited truce without a new alliance

outcome.text: You improve trust with {{other}}. The households do not acquire an alliance merely because the drinking is less hostile.

choices.label: Reply with a toast they cannot mistake

outcome.text: You gain a little charm and deepen the rivalry. {{other}} now has a sentence worth repeating accurately.

events.title: THE CHAPEL WITH YOUR NAME ON IT
events.text: {{other}} proposes a lavish family memorial while your household’s roof needs repair. The plan gives your name excellent shelter and your family rather less.

choices.label: Repair the living household first (18g)

outcome.text: You improve the household’s shelter and keep the memorial on paper. {{other}} finds the living family’s gratitude less artistically satisfying.

choices.label: Buy the public dedication instead (18g)

outcome.text: You pay for the dedication and gain family reputation. Your existing rooms do not become drier because a mason spells your name correctly.

choices.label: Defer both commissions

outcome.text: You preserve the coin and lose a little favour with {{other}}. The rain continues to make its own argument.

events.title: THE TASTER’S FINAL OBJECTION
events.text: Your taster refuses a cup offered by {{other}}. The objection is unusually specific: the same mixture killed the rats behind the kitchen.

choices.label: Have the cup removed and preserve it as evidence

outcome.text: You avoid the danger and make {{other}} a rival. No conviction follows merely from your suspicion.

choices.label: Drink to demonstrate confidence (risk death)

success.text: The drink is merely foul. Your confidence impresses the room and injures your health, which has not been asked for an opinion.

failure.text: The taster was right about the mixture. Royal confidence cannot persuade your body to survive it.

effects.death: Died after drinking a cup explicitly suspected of poison.

choices.label: Pay for an independent inquiry (15 treasury)

outcome.text: You fund an inquiry and improve public order. {{other}} resents a suspicion that now has a budget.

events.title: THE AUCTION OF YOUR SUCCESSION
events.text: {{other}} asks what it would cost to become your heir. The offer is accompanied by a list of improvements to your eventual funeral.

choices.label: Reject the purchase and publish the approach

outcome.text: You improve Crown standing and make a rival of {{other}}. The funeral improvements are returned without comment.

choices.label: Take a personal payment without changing the succession

outcome.text: You pocket thirty gold and leave the succession untouched. {{other}} keeps quiet for now; the payment is recorded as a bribe, not a claim.

charge.offence: Taking a bribe over a promised succession

choices.label: Abdicate to the documented eligible successor

outcome.text: You surrender the crown through the recorded succession. {{other}} receives no special appointment for having brought a price list.

events.title: THE LIGHTER ROYAL FACE
events.text: {{other}} proposes lightening the coin while leaving your portrait large enough to inspire confidence. The proposed saving is almost entirely silver.

choices.label: Keep the standard and publish the accounts

outcome.text: You improve public order and Crown standing. {{other}} abandons the suggestion that your face could replace a metal.

choices.label: Order the dishonest issue

outcome.text: The royal treasury gains forty gold while public order and family standing fall. The accusation of fraud bears your seal as clearly as the coins bear your face.

charge.offence: Ordering a dishonest issue of coin

choices.label: Fund relief instead (20 treasury)

outcome.text: You spend twenty treasury gold on relief and improve food security. {{other}} sees money leave the account without becoming any lighter.

events.title: THE VERDICT DELIVERED BEFORE THE WITNESSES
events.text: {{other}} asks you to approve a private condemnation before hearing evidence. It would save the council a morning. The saving is offered as a reason to take a life.

choices.label: Require evidence and leave the person alive

outcome.text: You refuse the execution and improve public order. {{other}} loses trust in your willingness to make justice convenient.

choices.label: Condemn the named petitioner instead (death and a family feud)

outcome.text: You order {{other}}’s death. The person dies, public order falls and the household feud outlives the audience.

familyFeud.reason: A summary royal execution without evidence

choices.label: Dismiss the petition without deciding the case

outcome.text: You leave the accusation unproved and gain a little public standing. {{other}} has saved neither a morning nor an enemy.

events.title: THE SAINT’S SMALLER SKULL
events.text: {{other}} displays a saint’s skull beside a smaller skull said to belong to the saint as a child. The keeper has anticipated the obvious objection and looks tired of it.

choices.label: Ask for the history of both objects

outcome.text: You expose the weak account without inventing a miracle. Your reputation improves and {{other}} becomes less welcoming to questions.

choices.label: Leave the objects and give alms instead (4g)

outcome.text: You give four gold toward relief rather than the display. Your faith and family standing improve without acquiring an extra saint.

choices.label: Write an endorsement you know is false

outcome.text: You lend your name to the false display and create a fraud charge. The smaller skull has acquired an adult witness.

events.title: THE ANIMAL DECLARED A FISH
events.text: {{other}} supports declaring a barnyard animal a fish so it may be eaten on fast days. The proposed proof is that it has once stood in a puddle.

choices.label: Ask why the puddle did not convert its owner

outcome.text: You gain public wit and lose {{other}}’s affection. The argument is not improved by your willingness to test it.

choices.label: Keep the fast without policing everyone’s supper

outcome.text: You keep your own observance and improve your relationship with {{other}} by declining to turn a meal into a trial.

events.title: THE OVEN OF INNOCENCE
events.text: {{other}} wants to settle an accusation by having you touch a heated oven door. The oven is said to know the truth. Nobody has explained how it will communicate it.

choices.label: Demand witnesses rather than an injury

outcome.text: You refuse the ordeal, gain public standing and lose {{other}}’s favour. The oven remains available for bread.

choices.label: Submit to the burning ordeal (lasting pain)

outcome.text: You burn your hand and develop chronic pain. {{other}} admires your endurance. The admiration does nothing for the hand.

choices.label: Pay for a formal petition instead (11g)

outcome.text: You pay to have your objection heard through ordinary testimony. Crown standing improves without the heat being mistaken for evidence.

events.title: THE PILGRIMAGE MEASURED IN RENT
events.text: {{other}} offers to make a pilgrimage on your behalf for a fee determined by how sinful you look. The route gets longer as you explain your finances.

choices.label: Make a modest local pilgrimage yourself

outcome.text: You spend your strength rather than money and gain faith. {{other}} loses a customer but cannot lengthen your road.

choices.label: Contribute to a genuine traveller’s expenses (7g)

outcome.text: You give seven gold without claiming that another person’s miles cancel your conduct. {{other}} appreciates an honest purpose for the journey.

choices.label: Decline the spiritual distance calculation

outcome.text: You ask whether the return journey also reduces your sins. {{other}} decides that your soul requires a different sort of customer.

events.title: THE FUNERAL’S PRICE OF SILENCE
events.text: {{other}} is collecting for a neighbour’s burial. The fee for leaving out an embarrassing story is higher than the fee for telling any number of flattering ones.

choices.label: Pay toward a plain, respectful burial (5g)

outcome.text: You give five gold toward the burial and improve family standing. The dead are not made more virtuous by being more expensive.

choices.label: Refuse to pay for withholding gossip

outcome.text: You challenge the charge and lose {{other}}’s affection. Your own reputation improves for making the objection before anyone starts the story.

choices.label: Supply a better story to lower your share

outcome.text: You spread private gossip and gain a rival in {{other}}, who no longer trusts you with an account that might reach the next funeral.

events.title: THE KEY TO CHARITY
events.text: {{other}} holds the key to a food chest and insists it cannot be opened until the donors’ names are read. Hungry people are waiting through an exceptionally generous list.

choices.label: Offer to read the names while food is served

outcome.text: You help the distribution without emptying your own household stores. Church standing and {{other}}’s trust improve.

choices.label: Supply food from your own household reserve

outcome.text: Your household gives up food and gains reputation. {{other}} sees a donation delivered without first hearing its name.

choices.label: Make a public account of the delay

outcome.text: You improve Commons standing and make {{other}} a rival. The key’s owner learns that waiting can be recorded too.

events.title: THE MIRACLE OF THE DRY PARCHMENT
events.text: Rain avoids the shrine’s best account book because {{other}} keeps it under the only sound section of roof. The rest of the room is being called a test of faith.

choices.label: Fund repairs instead of another miracle plaque (10g)

outcome.text: You improve your household’s standing through the contribution and gain Church favour. The work is paid for by coin, without claiming an unbuilt roof has already risen.

choices.label: Point out the useful location of the ledger

outcome.text: You gain wit and lose {{other}}’s patience. The book remains impressively dry.

events.title: THE BRIDGE THAT REQUIRES FAITH
events.text: {{other}} promises that a saint protects those crossing a broken footbridge. A long detour exists, which has made the promise commercially inconvenient.

choices.label: Take the long, safe road

outcome.text: You lose some strength to the detour and gain a little faith in the value of reaching your destination.

choices.label: Trust the damaged bridge (risk drowning)

success.text: You cross safely and gain a modest reputation for nerve. The missing boards have not been repaired by your example.

failure.text: The bridge gives way over deep water. The assurance of protection cannot keep you afloat.

effects.death: Drowned after choosing to cross a visibly broken bridge.

choices.label: Warn travellers and refuse to endorse the assurance

outcome.text: You improve public order by challenging the dangerous claim. {{other}} acquires a rival who knows exactly which boards are missing.

events.title: THE SERMON WITH YOUR MEASURES IN IT
events.text: {{other}} has proposed a sermon against dishonest measures using details suspiciously close to your neighbours’ accounts. You are asked to confirm the names.

choices.label: Insist that accusations require evidence

outcome.text: You improve public standing and lose {{other}}’s confidence in your willingness to make an example of someone.

choices.label: Confirm names you cannot substantiate

outcome.text: You acquire a false-testimony charge. The sermon’s moral certainty has become your legal uncertainty.

choices.label: Help write a sermon without identifying households

outcome.text: You preserve the moral point and improve Church standing. {{other}} discovers that an argument can survive without a named victim.

events.title: THE BROTHER WHO WILL NOT SPEAK
events.text: A visiting brother remains silent while {{other}} tries to extract a public blessing. The brother quietly helps an exhausted porter lift a load instead.

choices.label: Help carry the load without arranging a ceremony

outcome.text: You spend some strength and gain faith. {{other}} joins you after finding there is nobody left to applaud.

choices.label: Let the useful silence remain useful

outcome.text: You gain understanding without demanding a sign. {{other}} is less annoyed once no one is watching the disappointment.

events.title: THE RELIC WITH TOOTH MARKS
events.text: {{other}} asks you to help identify a sacred bone. The household dog identifies it first and is proving difficult to cross-examine.

choices.label: Withdraw the claim until there is evidence

outcome.text: You improve Church standing by declining to manufacture certainty. {{other}} is disappointed that the dog will not be treated as a witness for the defence.

choices.label: Turn the gathering toward ordinary alms (3g)

outcome.text: You contribute three gold to relief and gain faith. The bone’s status remains undecided while something useful happens.

events.title: THE WINDOW OPENED IN WINTER
events.text: {{other}} wants a dying neighbour visited but objects to the draught from the open door. The objection has outlasted the visitor’s strength.

choices.label: Visit and bring something warm (4g)

outcome.text: You spend four gold on care and gain faith. {{other}} sees a useful duty completed before it can become another argument.

choices.label: Give a household blanket instead of debating the door

outcome.text: Your household loses a little wealth and gains a reputation for care. You do not claim to have cured the neighbour by being kind.

choices.label: Leave the discussion to people who have time for it

outcome.text: You avoid the expense and lose {{other}}’s respect. The unfinished duty is smaller than your explanation for leaving it.

events.title: THE SCAFFOLD’S BLESSING
events.text: {{other}} says the repaired scaffold has been blessed. The supporting peg is still lying on the ground beside the holy water.

choices.label: Fit the peg before going up

outcome.text: You spend the time securing the work and gain practical experience. {{other}} concedes that the blessing need not do every part of the job.

choices.label: Climb before the support is fixed (risk lasting injury)

success.text: The scaffold holds and you finish the task. You collect the promised fee for a task that remains a terrible example.

failure.text: The platform gives way. The fall leaves lasting pain that does not disappear when the bruises fade.

choices.label: Refuse to test the argument with your body

outcome.text: You keep your health and lose a little favour with {{other}}. The peg remains admirably available.

events.title: THE MAN WHO CAN POLISH YOUR SIGHT
events.text: {{other}} recommends a travelling healer who promises to polish your sight with an abrasive paste. The demonstration is being performed on a spoon.

choices.label: Refuse the treatment and rest your eyes

outcome.text: You gain a little health by resting. Any existing eye condition remains; the spoon’s recovery proves nothing about yours.

choices.label: Submit to the abrasive treatment (permanent eye damage)

outcome.text: The paste injures your eyes. Failing sight becomes a lasting disability, and {{other}} loses your trust.

choices.label: Demand evidence from a patient rather than cutlery

outcome.text: You improve public standing by challenging the claim. {{other}} learns that a polished spoon is not a testimonial.

events.title: THE WORK THAT WILL NOT SWEAT ITSELF
events.text: While you are feverish, {{other}} insists a hard day’s labour will drive the sickness out. You would prefer it to leave by a door that does not require lifting.

choices.label: Rest and accept a lost day’s work

outcome.text: You recover some health and lose a little work performance. The existing illness remains subject to its real course.

choices.label: Work through the fever (risk making it worse)

outcome.text: You lose health and the lung fever becomes more severe. {{other}} is impressed by an effort your body has not endorsed.

choices.label: Pay for practical help and keep resting (7g)

outcome.text: You pay for help and recover some strength without pretending the payment itself removes the disease.

events.title: THE SHORTCUT WITHOUT THE ROAD
events.text: {{other}} offers to show you a quicker descent through an abandoned quarry. It is certainly shorter; the question is whether you arrive in one piece.

choices.label: Stay on the long road

outcome.text: You spend strength on the safe route and lose some favour with the guide. The road continues to justify its existence.

choices.label: Take the narrow ledge (risk a fatal fall)

success.text: You reach the bottom unharmed and gain confidence. {{other}} claims the loose stones were part of the intended route.

failure.text: The ledge crumbles beneath you. The shorter route has no place to stop the fall.

effects.death: Killed after choosing a dangerous shortcut through an abandoned quarry.

choices.label: Turn back before the descent begins

outcome.text: You give up the excursion and preserve your health. {{other}} keeps the story of the shortcut for a more agreeable audience.

events.title: THE WHITE DUST UNDER THE LID
events.text: {{other}} asks you to open a hot lime vessel without waiting for it to cool. The warning on the lid is inconveniently short and clear.

choices.label: Wait for proper cooling and protection

outcome.text: You gain practical judgement and a little trust. {{other}} discovers that impatience is cheaper than a burn only until someone obeys it.

choices.label: Open the hot vessel (severe burns)

outcome.text: You suffer real burns and lose health. {{other}} can no longer call the warning an excess of caution.

events.title: THE FERRY’S EXTRA PASSENGER
events.text: {{other}} asks you to board a ferry already low in the water. The ferryman argues that the extra fare will make the crossing worthwhile.

choices.label: Wait for the next crossing

outcome.text: You miss the busy part of the market and lose a little work performance. Your feet remain on the useful side of the river.

choices.label: Board the overloaded ferry (risk drowning)

success.text: The ferry reaches the bank. You gain a small reputation for nerve and remain unable to spend it on better buoyancy.

failure.text: The overloaded boat capsizes in deep water. The extra fare cannot purchase a shore.

effects.death: Drowned after choosing an overloaded ferry.

choices.label: Pay to leave a cargo bundle behind (7g)

outcome.text: You pay for a safer arrangement and gain {{other}}’s respect. The ferryman reluctantly accepts that cargo can miss a crossing.

events.title: THE TWO IDENTICAL HERB BUNDLES
events.text: {{other}} has mixed up two bundles of herbs, one soothing and one violently unsuitable for supper. The labels were left in the other basket.

choices.label: Discard both and buy known food (4g)

outcome.text: You pay for ordinary food rather than an exciting diagnosis. {{other}} accepts the loss of the herbs.

choices.label: Taste a little to decide

outcome.text: The experiment causes gut sickness and costs you health. {{other}} learns the result without sharing the method.

choices.label: Leave both bundles untouched

outcome.text: You refuse the gamble and gain some judgement. Not every uncertain meal needs a conclusive ending.

events.title: THE BENCH BESIDE THE HEARTH
events.text: {{other}} has moved a small workbench beside the hearth while your bone heals. It is useful, and almost tactful enough not to mention being useful.

choices.label: Accept the help and work gently

outcome.text: You gain a little health and deepen trust with {{other}}. The broken bone remains real; the day becomes less difficult.

choices.label: Refuse to be treated as injured

outcome.text: You push too hard and lose health. {{other}} leaves the bench nearby without requiring you to admit anything.

events.title: THE CURE THAT IS MOSTLY A CHAIR
events.text: {{other}} recommends a chair beside the fire for your lasting pain. It is the first proposed remedy not accompanied by a promise to make you entirely new.

choices.label: Take the chair and accept limited relief

outcome.text: Your health improves a little while the chronic pain remains. {{other}} is good enough company not to call this a miracle.

choices.label: Keep working and refuse the fuss

outcome.text: You lose some health and gain a little work experience. The disability is neither cured nor turned into a moral failing.

events.title: THE TONIC WITH A FUNERAL GUARANTEE
events.text: {{other}} recommends a tonic whose seller promises a refund if it fails. The refund must be claimed in person, after burial.

choices.label: Decline the reassuring guarantee

outcome.text: You ask to see the guarantee in writing. {{other}} discovers a pressing appointment with someone who has not asked that question.

choices.label: Buy it despite the warning (6g)

outcome.text: You pay for a useless tonic and lose a little health. No disease is removed, and the guarantee remains admirably difficult to invoke.

choices.label: Read the condition to the waiting customers

outcome.text: You expose the trick and gain public standing. {{other}} is embarrassed to have supplied such a precise recommendation.

events.title: THE SICKROOM’S EXCELLENT WITNESS
events.text: {{other}} offers to swear you have recovered enough to work, even though your health is still poor. The employer is prepared to believe whoever costs less.

choices.label: Give an honest account of your limits

outcome.text: You lose work performance and gain trust with {{other}} by refusing a useful falsehood. Your health remains a fact rather than a certificate.

choices.label: Submit the false declaration

outcome.text: You gain a little performance at the cost of health and a fraud charge. The declaration has not repaired the body it describes.

charge.offence: Submitting a knowingly false fitness declaration

events.title: THE BANDAGE TIED TO A PROMISE
events.text: {{other}} helps dress your wound and asks you to remember the favour when less frightened. The knot is firmer than the request.

choices.label: Promise practical help when you are able

outcome.text: You gain a little health and a trustworthy bond. The wound remains under care rather than vanishing under a promise.

choices.label: Pay fairly instead of owing a favour (5g)

outcome.text: You pay five gold for the help and recover some strength. {{other}} accepts a small, completed kindness.

choices.label: Accept the help and dismiss the obligation

outcome.text: You gain some health and lose trust. {{other}} tightens the final knot in silence.

events.title: THE MAN WHO WILL CATCH THUNDER
events.text: {{other}} has arranged a public demonstration with an iron pole on a high roof during a storm. The fee for holding the pole is described as hazard money only after you ask.

choices.label: Refuse the roof and warn the onlookers

outcome.text: You preserve your life and gain public standing. {{other}} calls the crowd’s new distance a failure of confidence.

choices.label: Hold the pole through the storm (risk death)

success.text: The worst of the storm passes elsewhere. You earn twenty gold for a demonstration that has proved nothing safe.

failure.text: Lightning strikes the exposed roof. The promised hazard payment is no defence against it.

effects.death: Killed while knowingly holding an iron pole on a roof during a storm.

events.title: THE INHERITANCE THAT REQUIRES AN ADVANCE
events.text: {{other}} brings news of a vast foreign inheritance. The messenger requires an advance, a travel bond and your patience about the absence of a named deceased.

choices.label: Ask for an identified estate and witnesses

outcome.text: You refuse the unsupported claim and improve your judgement. {{other}} is suddenly less certain which country contains the fortune.

choices.label: Borrow heavily to fund the supposed claim

negative: A debt remains to be repaid

outcome.text: You record a sixty-gold debt and lose household wealth meeting the costs. No inheritance arrives to recognise the trouble you have taken.

choices.label: Give the demand to the clerk

outcome.text: You expose the scheme and gain public standing. {{other}} becomes a rival who can now name at least one person involved.

events.title: THE STATUE WITH A SORE THROAT
events.text: {{other}} shows you a statue said to speak through a hole in the wall. Behind the wall, somebody asks for water in exactly the statue’s voice.

choices.label: Open the door before the next revelation

outcome.text: You expose the trick and gain reputation. {{other}} is annoyed that the revelation has acquired a visible speaker.

choices.label: Leave without making the frightened audience a joke

outcome.text: You preserve your own judgement and gain faith through restraint. {{other}} is grateful for less discretion than they wanted.

choices.label: Offer a more convincing voice for a dishonest fee

outcome.text: You earn seven gold and a fraud charge. Your best performance now comes with a witness behind the wall.

charge.offence: Taking payment for a staged sacred revelation

events.title: THE HOUSE BUILT ROUND A BONE
events.text: {{other}} owns a sea creature’s enormous bone and wants to charge people to touch it for luck. The carpenter thinks it would make an excellent lintel.

choices.label: Study the bone without buying the promised luck

outcome.text: You learn something about its scale and improve your bond with {{other}}. The bone remains remarkable without an extra power.

choices.label: Contribute to a shelter display (6g)

outcome.text: Your contribution improves the family’s public standing. The contribution supports a display, not a miracle.

events.title: THE GAME WITH A KING WHO CANNOT LEAVE
events.text: {{other}} teaches you a foreign board game in which the king moves very little and everyone else is sacrificed around him. The explanation attracts an uncomfortable number of courtiers.

choices.label: Learn the game without supplying an allegory

outcome.text: You gain judgement and a friendly bond with {{other}}. The little king is allowed to remain a piece of wood.

choices.label: Explain which actual people the pieces resemble

outcome.text: You gain charm and make a rival of {{other}}, who did not intend the lesson to require a defence before witnesses.

events.title: THE DEVIL HAS TAKEN THE AFTERNOON OFF
events.text: The person playing the devil in a pageant has refused to perform until paid. {{other}} asks you to explain to the crowd why virtue has nothing left to conquer.

choices.label: Pay the performer what the organiser owes (9g)

outcome.text: You spend nine gold to help settle the dispute and improve public standing. The devil returns to work on unusually reasonable terms.

choices.label: Rewrite the ending around a missing adversary

outcome.text: You gain performance skill and help the show continue without claiming anyone has been paid. {{other}} discovers that goodness can be made to quarrel with itself.

choices.label: Blame the absent performer before the crowd

outcome.text: You damage {{other}}’s trust and lose public standing for turning an unpaid wage into a moral failing.

events.title: THE CASTLE THAT FITS IN A CHEST
events.text: {{other}} shows you a beautifully made model castle with working gates. It defends a table far more effectively than several actual castles defend their villages.

choices.label: Ask how the little gates were made

outcome.text: You gain practical experience and a warm bond with {{other}}. An evening passes without anybody trying to conquer anything.

choices.label: Ask how much grain the model has protected

outcome.text: You gain a little wit and damage the acquaintance. {{other}} closes a gate that, for once, could not have kept you out.

events.title: THE WORD FOR COMING HOME
events.text: {{other}} returns from a long journey and tries to explain a word for the relief of reaching a place that knows you. The closest translation takes the rest of supper.

choices.label: Let the explanation take as long as it needs

outcome.text: You gain understanding and a deeper bond. {{other}} eventually stops translating and asks for more bread.

choices.label: Share household food and let the word remain foreign

outcome.text: You give up a little food and gain a warm acquaintance. Some meanings travel more easily in company than in words.

events.title: THE BAILIFF’S FOURTH CHICKEN
events.text: The bailiff demands a hen that your household has never owned. Your family contact has the old rent tally.

choices.label: Compare the bailiff’s rent tally

outcome.text: You and your neighbour prove the tally. The hen remains imaginary; the debt does not grow.

choices.label: Accept the bailiff’s hush money

outcome.text: The bailiff pays you three coins to hide his extra assessment. Your household loses more grain than those coins could buy.

events.title: THE GUILD’S SMALL PRINT
events.text: Your family’s commission includes a penalty for hammer noise after compline. The church commissioned the bell.

choices.label: Ask {{contact}} to check the guild exemption

outcome.text: Your guild contact finds the exemption. The household keeps its fee.

choices.label: Keep the noise penalty secret for three gold

outcome.text: You pocket three gold while the workshop pays the penalty. {{contact}} learns whose silence was purchased.

events.title: THE RIVAL’S SHORT BUSHEL
events.text: The household’s rival sells grain in a bushel with a false bottom. Your parent asks you to watch the measure.

choices.label: Ask {{contact}} to witness the false measure

outcome.text: You bring witnesses and protect the household’s buyers. The rival now knows your name.

choices.label: Take three gold from the short-measure seller

outcome.text: The seller buys your silence. Your household’s buyers discover the short grain and blame the family name.

events.title: THE LAY SCRIBE’S BABY
events.text: A visiting friar mistakes your lay scribe parent for a vowed cleric and prepares a scandal of magnificent proportions.

choices.label: Produce the household marriage entry

outcome.text: The marriage entry settles it. The friar must find his scandal elsewhere.

choices.label: Sell the friar a rumour for three gold

outcome.text: The friar pays for a scandal about your own lay household. The correction will cost considerably more than three gold.

events.title: THE RATION HEIR
events.text: The garrison refuses to feed a soldier’s child until the child can carry a spear. The spear is taller than the clerk.

choices.label: Ask {{contact}} to cite the service oath

outcome.text: Your household contact quotes the service oath. You receive bread and an enemy in the stores.

choices.label: Take three gold to abandon the ration claim

outcome.text: The stores clerk buys your silence. Your family gives up a season of bread for your private handful of coins.

events.title: THE COUSIN’S LITTLE MAP
events.text: A cousin has drawn the family boundary through your nursery. The steward offers to charge you rent.

choices.label: Ask {{contact}} to compare the boundary charter

outcome.text: You compare the charter with the stones. The cousin loses a field and a little affection.

choices.label: Accept three gold to hide the cousin’s map

outcome.text: Your cousin buys your silence and presses the boundary claim. The household discovers your price was lower than the surveyor’s.

events.title: THE NURSERY PRECEDENT
events.text: Your older sibling claims the whole nursery under a succession custom invented before breakfast.

choices.label: Ask the guardian to settle nursery precedence

outcome.text: Your guardian divides the room. The throne remains undivided and very far away.

choices.label: Sell your sibling the secret nursery key

outcome.text: Your sibling pays three gold for the nursery key. The guards change the locks and your household’s opinion of you.

events.title: THE FLOODED STRIP
events.text: {{guardian}} finds seed floating across a neighbour’s boundary. {{contact}} remembers where the old ditch ran.

choices.label: Reopen the ditch together

outcome.text: The reopened ditch saves seed on both strips. {{contact}} records your household’s share of the labour.

choices.label: Charge the neighbour for your own lost seed

outcome.text: Your false claim wins a few coins and leaves {{guardian}} to repair the damaged neighbourly agreement.

events.title: THE WINTER WOOD
events.text: {{contact}} offers fallen wood if your household helps mend the common gate before winter.

choices.label: Help {{guardian}} mend the gate

outcome.text: The common gate stands through winter. {{contact}} delivers the promised fallen wood.

choices.label: Sell the gate timber secretly

outcome.text: The missing timber leaves the common gate open. {{contact}} charges your household for its replacement.

events.title: THE CUSTOMER’S SEAL
events.text: {{guardian}} has a commission without a deposit. {{contact}} recognises the customer’s disputed seal.

choices.label: Ask for a witnessed deposit

outcome.text: The witnessed deposit pays for material before the customer can dispute the order.

choices.label: Copy the seal onto another order

outcome.text: The copied seal is discovered on the second order. {{contact}} keeps it as evidence against your household.

events.title: THE GUILD FEAST
events.text: {{contact}} invites your household to show a trial piece. The entry fee will buy a week’s supper.

choices.label: Help {{guardian}} prepare a modest sample

outcome.text: The modest sample gives the workshop a place at the feast without emptying its supper pot.

choices.label: Pass off another workshop’s piece

outcome.text: The borrowed trial piece is recognised. Your workshop pays the entry fee and loses the guild’s trust.

events.title: THE SHIPMENT AT THE FORD
events.text: {{guardian}} must choose between a safe crossing fee and a cheap flooded ford. {{contact}} has a wagon there too.

choices.label: Share the safe crossing cost

outcome.text: Both wagons share the safe crossing and split the fee. The shipment arrives with its partners intact.

choices.label: Send {{contact}} toward the flooded ford

outcome.text: {{contact}} finds the dangerous ford and learns who gave the directions. Your household loses a trading partner.

events.title: THE LEDGER’S SECOND HAND
events.text: A rival disputes {{guardian}}’s ledger. {{contact}} offers to witness a recount in the market.

choices.label: Carry both copies to the recount

outcome.text: The recount establishes what was delivered. The rival must challenge a witnessed account.

choices.label: Remove the page that favours the rival

outcome.text: The missing ledger page becomes the rival’s strongest evidence. Your household bears the cost of your bargain.

events.title: THE BORROWED MANUSCRIPT
events.text: {{guardian}} owes the priory a manuscript. {{contact}} finds rain beneath the reading-room window.

choices.label: Help dry and recopy the damaged leaves

outcome.text: The dried leaves and careful copies satisfy the priory. Your lay household retains its access to the books.

choices.label: Blame a visiting lay household

outcome.text: The visiting household produces witnesses. Your own household pays for the damaged manuscript.

events.title: THE CHARITY BREAD
events.text: {{contact}} asks your household to record bread for hungry neighbours. One loaf remains after the tally.

choices.label: Ask {{guardian}} to check the names

outcome.text: The checked names reveal a hungry neighbour missed from the tally. The last loaf reaches them.

choices.label: Sell the extra loaf and alter the list

outcome.text: The altered bread list is traced to your hand. Your household must replace what the charity lost.

events.title: THE OLD CAMPAIGN CLOAK
events.text: {{guardian}} offers a service cloak for your first training. {{contact}} notices an unpaid campaign receipt in its lining.

choices.label: Return the receipt to the pay clerk

outcome.text: The pay clerk acknowledges the old receipt and credits the service household.

choices.label: Forge an extra ration claim

outcome.text: The extra ration is refused when {{contact}} checks the muster. Your household’s genuine claim is delayed.

events.title: THE GARRISON’S HORSE
events.text: {{contact}} needs someone to hold a nervous horse while {{guardian}} checks its harness.

choices.label: Help check the girth and stay beside it

outcome.text: The checked girth holds and the garrison records your household’s help.

choices.label: Tell the quartermaster another child lost it

outcome.text: The quartermaster finds your false account beside the harness. Your household loses standing with the stores.

events.title: THE EMPTY TUTOR’S PURSE
events.text: {{guardian}} must meet a tutor’s fee and a tenant’s request for seed. {{contact}} has the household accounts.

choices.label: Read the accounts before asking for more

outcome.text: The accounts show what can be spent on tutors after seed is reserved. Your guardian trusts you with the next petition.

choices.label: Hide the tenant’s petition

outcome.text: The hidden petition is found. The tenants blame your household for a refusal it never openly made.

events.title: THE COUSIN AT TABLE
events.text: {{contact}} brings a cousin’s challenge to your household’s precedence. {{guardian}} asks you to carry the family record.

choices.label: Present the record without insults

outcome.text: The family record settles precedence without an insult. Your cousin has less reason to press another grievance.

choices.label: Alter the cousin’s place in the record

outcome.text: The altered genealogy reaches {{contact}}. The cousin keeps a copy and begins a more serious challenge.

events.title: THE TWO NURSERY SEALS
events.text: {{guardian}} finds rival nursery orders signed by different palace factions. {{contact}} asks which order you carried.

choices.label: Show both seals to the guardian

outcome.text: Both nursery seals reach the guardian. Conflicting orders are corrected before the guards choose sides.

choices.label: Tell each faction the other threatened you

outcome.text: The two palace factions compare your stories. Both now have grounds to distrust your household’s word.

events.title: THE HEIR’S LESSON
events.text: {{guardian}} arranges a lesson beside your elder sibling. {{contact}} says guards have begun wagering on which of you will rule.

choices.label: Share the lesson and refuse the wager

outcome.text: The shared lesson gives the guards no wager to collect. Your guardian records a rare quiet agreement between heirs.

choices.label: Buy a guard’s rumour about your sibling

outcome.text: The purchased rumour reaches your sibling. A nursery quarrel acquires a guard willing to repeat it.

events.title: THE FIRST HOUSEHOLD WORDS
events.text: Avice counts cups at supper. You repeat the word for cup with greater confidence than accuracy.

choices.label: Count the cups together

outcome.text: Your household gains a small voice in its nightly accounting. The cups remain easier to count than the debts.

choices.label: Insist the cat is also a cup

outcome.text: The cat refuses to join the crockery. Your household repeats the word more slowly.

events.title: RAIN OVER THE CRADLE
events.text: Rain finds a gap over your bedding. The household has one dry blanket and several strong opinions about the roof.

choices.label: Carry a small bowl to catch the rain

outcome.text: The bowl catches a little water. Your guardian praises the help and moves your bedding somewhere dry.

choices.label: Ask to share the dry blanket

outcome.text: Your guardian folds the dry blanket around you. The roof will require a less comfortable remedy.

events.title: YOUR RIVAL HAS HIRED A DRUMMER
events.text: {{rival.name}} marches into the market behind a drummer and announces that you fight like a wet pillow. A merchant offers a 30g prize if you win. Your rival demands a 10g entry wager. The drummer has learned exactly one beat.

choices.label: Take the challenge (10g)
choices.hint: Play a four-exchange duel. Win: 30g prize and duel honours. Lose or yield: your wager is gone. Injuries and reputation are at stake.

stakes.summary: Wager paid: 10g. Win the 30g purse and duel honours. Lose or yield: no refund; injury and reputation loss.

outcome.text: The merchant holds your wager. The drummer discovers a second beat. You step into the ring.

choices.label: Challenge the drummer to learn a second beat

outcome.text: The crowd laughs. The drummer stops. Your rival must now provide their own dramatic entrance.

choices.label: Keep your gold and walk away

outcome.text: You leave the wet-pillow debate to the experts. Your purse remains undefeated.

events.title: THE GRAIN CART CHAMPION
events.text: {{challenger.name}} blocks the grain cart and demands a fight before letting it pass. The driver offers you 12g to clear the road. The challenger has painted a crown on a bucket and is wearing it.

choices.label: Fight for the grain
choices.hint: Win: 12g and +15 Stores. Lose or yield: −10 Stores. Normal duel honours, injury and reputation also apply.

stakes.summary: Win: 12g and +15 Stores. Lose or yield: −10 Stores. Duel honours, injury and reputation also apply.

outcome.text: The driver lends you a blunted sword. The bucket king lowers the royal visor.

choices.label: Take the muddy detour

outcome.text: You lead the cart around the field. One sack gets soaked. The bucket king is left ruling an empty road.

events.title: THE WANDERING MONK
events.text: The travelling monk asks the children to copy “Do not waste parchment.” He has written it on a fresh sheet so large that even the back row can see the irony.

choices.label: Learn the letters, including the expensive ones

outcome.text: You learn enough letters to read the warning yourself. The monk lets you keep a scrap and looks away while you practise.

choices.label: Spend the lesson with Sir Quackbeard

outcome.text: The goose offers no instruction and requires no parchment. You enjoy the company, though the writing remains unread.

choices.label: Introduce the frog to the lesson

outcome.text: The frog leaves a wet impression on the page. You gain a reputation for mischief and the monk gains a very brief pupil with excellent jumping prospects.

events.title: A MOUNTAIN OF TURNIPS
events.text: {{father}} points out the rows waiting to be weeded. “You can see the end,” {{father}} says, omitting that the end is also where tomorrow begins.

choices.label: Work through the rows with your father

outcome.text: You finish tired and gain your father’s affection. The last row earns a quiet nod that nobody else would recognise as a celebration.

choices.label: Do enough, then hide in the hay

outcome.text: The nap is excellent. Your father’s disappointment is less restful and follows you indoors.

events.title: THE MILLER’S BIG SON
events.text: {{other}} collects lunches on behalf of the miller’s big son. The supposed protection consists of not being bothered by the people collecting it.

choices.label: Refuse the protection fee

success.text: You refuse to surrender lunch. {{other}} backs down and remembers exactly who made the collection difficult.

failure.text: You are knocked into the ditch. {{other}} keeps the food and acquires a rival who will remember more than the price of lunch.

choices.label: Surrender the lunch and keep the afternoon quiet

outcome.text: You hand over the food. {{other}} gains confidence in the arrangement and loses some of your trust.

choices.label: Call Sir Quackbeard between you

outcome.text: The goose drives {{other}} back by refusing to negotiate about ankles. The collection stops here, and the collector becomes a named rival.

events.title: THE QUACK DOCTOR
events.text: {{other}} offers a heated “healing stone” for six gold. The stone is ordinary; the explanation of its value requires a much rarer temperature.

choices.label: Buy the warmed stone (6g)

outcome.text: You pay for a warm stone and a rest beside the brazier. The rest helps a little; no illness is cured by the salesmanship.

choices.label: Ask what happens when the stone cools

outcome.text: {{other}} recommends another appointment. You decline with a better understanding of which part of the treatment needs constant warming.

choices.label: Take the stone without paying

outcome.text: You take the stone and create a theft complaint. It remains ordinary, but your legal record is now more interesting.

charge.offence: Taking a healer’s goods without payment

events.title: A RAT IN THE GRANARY
events.text: {{other}} has declared the granary’s rat an unofficial watchman because it frightens mice. The arrangement is paid entirely in your household’s winter grain.

choices.label: Remove the rat and mend the opening

outcome.text: You drive the rat out and repair the gap, losing a little blood to the work. Household stores and security improve under a watchman that is now a plank.

choices.label: Support the rat’s appointment

outcome.text: The household loses stored food and {{other}} likes you better. The rat’s performance improves in exactly the wrong direction.

choices.label: Blame Sir Quackbeard for the arrangement

outcome.text: You blame the goose and lose its affection. The opening remains unmended, so the household’s stores continue to suffer.

events.title: THE LORD’S TOURNEY
events.text: The tourney steward offers a discount entry because the horse is small. The opposing knight has not been discounted, which seems a serious omission.

choices.label: Enter the uneven joust (5g; risk injury)

success.text: You unhorse the opponent and earn a net eight gold after the entry fee. The steward objects only to how many people saw the small horse win.

failure.text: You land badly and leave with a real broken bone. The steward assures you that the entry fee included the fall.

choices.label: Sell pies where the losers come down

outcome.text: You earn nine gold supplying an audience with no shortage of dramatic landings. The best customers eat without taking their eyes off the field.

choices.label: Watch the horsemanship from the safe end

outcome.text: You study the riders without entering. A little judgement is gained without giving the healer a new customer.

events.title: CONFESSION TIME
events.text: The priest asks whether you have wronged anyone. You begin with a harmless example; the priest asks why you rehearsed that one first.

choices.label: Confess the inconvenient part as well

outcome.text: You admit the truth and gain faith. The admission does not settle debts or erase charges; it merely stops the priest waiting for the missing part.

choices.label: Claim a remarkably spotless conscience

outcome.text: You offer the account of a person nobody in the room has met. The priest hears you out, and you keep a secret about the omission.

choices.label: Give alms without pretending they answer the question (4g)

outcome.text: You give four gold and gain some faith. The priest accepts the donation and repeats the question, now that you have finished changing the subject.

events.title: A WANDERING KNIGHT
events.text: A travelling knight seeks someone to carry armour, remember messages and receive blame in that order. He calls the post an education, which suggests the wages will be small.

choices.label: Beg to be his squire

success.text: He grunted approval. You are on the path to knighthood, or at the very least to heavy lifting.

failure.text: He looked you up and down, sighed, and chose the blacksmith’s daughter instead.

choices.label: Ask what the work actually pays

outcome.text: You insist on a clear wage and receive five gold for a day carrying equipment. The knight leaves without an oath from you.

choices.label: Decline the offer without a quarrel

outcome.text: You decline the post. The road remains open, and you have not promised to carry someone else’s mistakes.

events.title: AN UNCANNY STREAK
events.text: You keep winning at dice. The other players have reached the point of blaming sorcery rather than their own arithmetic, a stage at which leaving may be the cleverest throw.

choices.label: Ride the luck for all it is worth

success.text: You cleaned out the whole table and walked home whistling, pockets jingling.

failure.text: Your luck finally blinked. You lost the lot, and a tooth, to a sore loser.

choices.label: Quit while you are ahead

outcome.text: You pocketed your winnings and left. The gamblers glared; fortune, like milk, can turn.

events.title: A CRUEL WINTER
events.text: The cold settles deep in your frail chest, as it always does. The herb-wife eyes you with pity and a price.

choices.label: Buy the strongest tonic (7g)

outcome.text: The tonic was vile and dear, but you saw the spring. For a sickly soul, that is a victory. The herb-wife now greets you by name across the market, which is not the compliment it sounds like.

choices.label: Endure it by the hearth

success.text: You wrapped in every blanket you own and outlasted the cold. Barely.

failure.text: The fever took hold and very nearly took you. You emerge in spring, hollow-eyed, with a cough that never entirely leaves.

events.title: THE SWEATING SICKNESS
events.text: A real fever has reached your household. The herb-wife is frank about what she can attempt, which makes her prices less comforting and her advice more credible.

choices.label: Pay the herb-wife at once (6g)

outcome.text: Her tonic is bitter but swift. The fever breaks before it can take root.

choices.label: Sweat it out and pray

success.text: You sweated through three foul nights and woke clear-eyed. Spared, this time.

failure.text: The fever digs in for the long haul. This sickness will not pass quickly.

events.title: THE REEVE COMES KNOCKING
events.text: The reeve’s men bring questions about your misdeeds. One has brought irons in case the answers prove inconvenient; the other has brought a receipt book.

choices.label: Bribe your way out (15g)

outcome.text: A heavy purse changes hands. The reeve discovers he was quite mistaken. Funny, that.

choices.label: Make a run for it

success.text: Out the back and over three fences. Free, filthy, and faster than you look.

failure.text: They caught you at the treeline and clapped you in irons.

choices.label: Surrender with dignity

outcome.text: You go quietly. The dungeon door clangs shut behind you.

events.title: A MATCH IS PROPOSED
events.text: A matchmaker offers an introduction to someone kind, capable and tired of being valued by the contents of a dowry chest. Consent, rather than a wedding, is the first business.

choices.label: Consent to the proposed household match

outcome.text: You marry by mutual consent and welcome a real spouse into the household. The settlement begins a life together, not a transfer of somebody’s belongings.

choices.label: Hold out for nobility

outcome.text: You spurned the match, eyes fixed on a grander union. Ambitious. Possibly foolish.

choices.label: Decline the match without insulting the suitor

outcome.text: You refuse kindly and leave the other person free to choose another life. No animal is required to explain the decision.

events.title: AN INVITATION TO THE HALL
events.text: You are invited to the high table after an account of your wit reaches the steward. It arrives slightly improved. You must now live up to something you never quite said.

choices.label: Charm the whole table

success.text: You had them roaring with laughter. The lord himself toasted you. Doors are opening.

failure.text: You used the wrong spoon, then the wrong fork, then insulted a baroness. A long carriage ride home.

choices.label: Quietly observe and learn

outcome.text: You said little and watched much. You now know who hates whom, and that is power.

events.title: A RIVAL AT COURT
events.text: {{other}} dismisses your success as an accident of useful acquaintances. The charge is delivered to as many useful acquaintances as possible.

choices.label: Expose the contradiction in the rumour

success.text: You make {{other}} answer for the contradictory story. Your reputation rises and the rivalry becomes explicit.

failure.text: Your trap contradicts your own account. {{other}} gains an advantage and a clearer reason to keep the rivalry alive.

choices.label: Buy a pause in the rumour (12g)

outcome.text: You pay twelve gold and gain a brief respite. {{other}} learns that silence has a price worth remembering.

choices.label: Challenge the rumour in public

outcome.text: You demand an answer before witnesses. {{other}} becomes a named rival instead of a rumour without an address.

events.title: A NOBLE PROPOSAL
events.text: {{other}} proposes a marriage of mutual advantage and asks what sort of life you would want beyond the advantage. It is the first question not answered by the settlement.

choices.label: Accept the proposed marriage

outcome.text: You marry into a better-connected household. Your standing can improve through that connection; no title is granted merely by the wedding.

choices.label: Decline without humiliating the suitor

outcome.text: You refuse the match graciously. Your reputation improves because you leave the proposal as private as it can still be.

events.title: THE NIGHT VIGIL
events.text: To be dubbed a knight you must keep an overnight vigil in the cold chapel, armour on, praying till dawn.

choices.label: Endure the full vigil

success.text: You knelt unmoving till dawn, half-frozen and wholly resolved. The bishop is impressed.

failure.text: You nodded off and clattered to the floor at midnight. Mortifying, but you finished anyway.

choices.label: Sneak a flask of wine for warmth

outcome.text: The wine kept you warm and the vigil bearable. The bishop suspects nothing. The goose would be proud.

events.title: A CHALLENGE OF HONOUR
events.text: Sir Roderick produces a glove for a challenge of honour. The careful preparation suggests he has been finding the original quarrel insufficiently productive.

choices.label: Accept the duel (risk a serious cut)

success.text: You disarm Roderick and stop with the weapon at his throat. He remains alive, humiliated and much less likely to call the next quarrel accidental.

failure.text: Roderick cuts you badly. The injury is real; your refusal to pretend it was a victory earns a small measure of respect.

choices.label: Refuse. It is beneath you

outcome.text: You called the challenge childish and walked away. Some respect the restraint. Roderick crows victory.

choices.label: Propose a contest of wits instead

outcome.text: You out-argued him so thoroughly the crowd laughed Roderick out of the square. A bloodless rout.

events.title: THE LORD’S SUMMONS
events.text: Your liege calls a muster over a disputed river crossing. The written claim is dry; the crossing, you are warned, will not be.

choices.label: Ride to war for your liege

outcome.text: You don your armour and ride out. The road to glory is muddy and smells of fear.

choices.label: Send coin in your stead (20g)

outcome.text: You paid scutage to avoid the muster. Pragmatic, if not glorious. Some call it cowardice.

events.title: THE PEASANTS’ PETITION
events.text: Tenants bring a petition against a levy assessed on roofs, including two roofs that fell in last winter. Your steward calls the assessment consistent.

choices.label: Fund relief from the harsh assessment

outcome.text: You pay for relief and improve loyalty. Your household gives up coin and stores; the tenants receive an answer they can survive.

choices.label: Enforce the assessment without relief

outcome.text: Your coffers grow as household loyalty and stores fall. The cruelty is recorded in your reputation rather than blamed on a parent who may not be alive.

choices.label: Offer a smaller assessment and clear terms

outcome.text: You take a smaller return and improve loyalty. People can plan around an amount that no longer changes with the steward’s mood.

events.title: A WHISPER OF TREASON
events.text: Plotters invite you to lend your name and evidence against a powerful baron. They promise to share the reward and are less exact about whose neck secures the attempt.

choices.label: Join the conspiracy

success.text: Your evidence reaches the council and the plotters pay you fifty gold. The baron faces an inquiry; no new title has yet been granted.

failure.text: The plot was betrayed. Guards drag you to the block at dawn.

effects.death: Beheaded for treason. The crowd, as ever, brought pies.

choices.label: Betray the plotters to the baron

outcome.text: You sold them out. The baron rewards your "loyalty" handsomely, though you sleep with one eye open now.

choices.label: Refuse without inventing a later victory

outcome.text: You keep your name off the conspiracy. What the plotters do next is theirs; your legal record does not acquire their plan.

events.title: BUILDING A LEGACY
events.text: A mason offers a public dedication worthy of your wealth. The relief wardens ask whether the money might also do something for people who cannot read the inscription.

choices.label: Fund chapel relief and a public dedication (40g)

outcome.text: You endow relief associated with the chapel. Food security and Church standing improve; the dedication does not pretend a new building rose in an afternoon.

choices.label: Fund care for the sick and poor (40g)

outcome.text: You pay for practical relief and improve public health conditions. The people doing the work receive supplies rather than an expensive drawing of a hospital.

choices.label: Keep the reserve for your household

outcome.text: You retain the money and improve the household’s food reserve by careful planning. There will be no inscription recording the choice.

events.title: A PEDLAR OF RELICS
events.text: A pedlar offers a supposedly angelic feather. The story is magnificent; the object is the sort a barnyard bird leaves without an audience.

choices.label: Buy it faithfully (8g)

outcome.text: You bought the feather and prayed over it nightly. Faith asks no questions. Strangely, you feel comforted.

choices.label: Expose him as a fraud

success.text: You show why the feather is an ordinary bird’s feather. Your reputation improves and {{other}} loses your trust rather than vanishing from the town.

failure.text: Your objection fails to convince the onlookers. {{other}} keeps the advantage and you keep the memory of being contradicted by people who never examined the feather.

choices.label: Steal it for the goose

outcome.text: You take the feather for Sir Quackbeard, who does not recognise a need to have it back. {{other}} has a genuine theft to complain about.

charge.offence: Taking a relic seller’s goods without payment

events.title: A CALLING TO THE CLOISTER
events.text: The abbot offers you holy orders, long work and a small place in a community that will know when you are avoiding either. You are allowed time to answer.

choices.label: Take the vows and duties

outcome.text: You take holy orders and gain Church standing. The vows do not appoint you to a paid post; service and qualifications must still earn one.

choices.label: Decline while offering ordinary help

outcome.text: You decline the vows and offer practical service. The abbot accepts an honest answer more readily than a beautiful promise.

events.title: A VILLAGER CRIES MIRACLE
events.text: A child’s recovery is being attributed to your nearby prayer. The people praising you have forgotten the person who carried water through the night.

choices.label: Accept the attention and its donations

outcome.text: You receive donations and public standing. The prayer is remembered, together with your willingness to stand beside its collection bowl.

choices.label: Credit the care and decline the claim

outcome.text: You insist that care deserves thanks as well as prayer. Church standing improves; you do not manufacture a new miracle to explain your humility.

events.title: A MOTHER TAKES ILL
events.text: {{mother}} is seriously ill. The herb-wife offers a costly treatment without a promise. Your mother objects to the expense before allowing herself to ask whether it might work.

choices.label: Fund the uncertain treatment (15g; she may die)

success.text: The treatment succeeds. {{mother}} recovers enough to complain about the fee, a sound you had been afraid of never hearing again.

failure.text: The treatment cannot save {{mother}}. You stay beside the bed and hold a hand no amount of spending can keep warm.

choices.label: Offer care and prayer without the treatment (she may die)

success.text: The fever breaks. {{mother}} credits your company before discussing anybody’s theology.

failure.text: {{mother}} dies despite the care you can give. You do not mistake being unable to pay for having been unwilling to love.

events.title: A CHILD IS BORN
events.text: A child has arrived in your household. The smallest person in the room has reorganised every task without speaking a comprehensible word.

choices.label: Welcome the child with joy

outcome.text: A healthy babe joins your household and your line continues. You weep, then panic about feeding it.

choices.label: Welcome the child quietly

outcome.text: You keep the first days close to the household, making promises before making announcements.

events.title: AN OLD FOE, HUMBLED
events.text: Sir Roderick appears at your door, greyer and smaller and short of a manor. "I... was wrong about you," he mutters. "About the apple. About all of it."

choices.label: Forgive him at last

outcome.text: You clasp his hand. Decades of grudge dissolve in a moment. He weeps; so, secretly, do you.

choices.label: Hand him a single apple, and shut the door

outcome.text: You give him one apple. "Now we are even," you say. The door closes. Petty? Perhaps. Satisfying? Immensely.

events.title: A SQUALLING ARRIVAL
events.text: Your mother sits you down with a strange smile. By harvest, you will not be the only small person in this cottage.

choices.label: Rejoice! A playmate at last

outcome.text: A sibling is born! Loud, wrinkled, and immediately beloved. You vow to teach them everything about turnips.

choices.label: Sulk about sharing the porridge

outcome.text: A sibling is born anyway. You sulk magnificently, but the baby grips your finger and your cold heart thaws a little.

events.title: THE SMITH’S CHILD
events.text: Another child keeps finding reasons to pass your fence. Today the reason is a pebble that has been kicked in the same small circle for most of the morning.
