events.text: {{client}} asks you to inspect wages paid to a dead falconer. {{rival}} suggests the hawks remain loyal enough to justify a pension.

choices.label: Publish the checked accounts

outcome.text: The burial entry and wage account are checked before publication.

choices.label: Confront the beneficiary immediately

outcome.text: The beneficiary is confronted before every payment has been traced.

choices.label: Ask another auditor to witness the books

outcome.text: A second auditor signs the checked account beside your name.

events.title: EXAMINE A PATIENT
events.text: {{client}} requests an examination. Establish actual symptoms first; a healthy person needs advice rather than an invented disease.

choices.label: Compare actual symptoms and history

outcome.text: Your examination begins with the person’s own history and observable signs.

choices.label: Give a rapid confident opinion

outcome.text: You give a rapid opinion and accept responsibility for its certainty.

choices.label: Consult another practitioner

outcome.text: Another practitioner reviews the observations before an opinion is recorded.

events.title: TREAT A HOUSEHOLD
events.text: {{client}} requests care based on the recorded symptoms. Relief depends on the real condition, your preparation and the risks of your method.

choices.label: Treat the recorded condition cautiously

outcome.text: Your care follows the actual record and avoids an unnecessary intervention.

choices.label: Attempt an aggressive intervention

outcome.text: You accept the greater risks of a forceful intervention for a hoped-for recovery.

choices.label: Arrange supervised care and follow-up

outcome.text: A colleague joins the care plan and agrees a follow-up examination.

events.title: ORGANISE FEVER RELIEF
events.text: {{client}} asks you to organise fever relief. The sick households share water, bedding and several contradictory explanations.

choices.label: Trace sick households and clean water

outcome.text: The relief plan traces sick households and the water they share.

choices.label: Order a public purge of suspect goods

outcome.text: A public order calls for suspect goods to be removed before the cause is fully established.

choices.label: Organise parish volunteers and beds

outcome.text: Volunteers arrange beds, clean cloth and separate drinking vessels.

events.title: PERFORM IN THE HALL
events.text: {{client}} offers a place in the hall’s programme. The audience likes a fine genealogy and dislikes finding its own scandals in the rhyme.

choices.label: Prepare a piece suited to the audience

outcome.text: You prepare a piece for the audience’s tastes and its known sensitivities.

choices.label: Improvise for a larger purse

outcome.text: You improvise before listeners whose generosity is not assured.

choices.label: Share the bill with another performer

outcome.text: The fellow performer receives an agreed place and share of the bill.

events.title: SEEK A PAYING PATRON
events.text: {{client}} is considering a place for a performer at their table. Supper, a deposit and the patron’s right to request encores all remain negotiable.

choices.label: Offer a documented service

outcome.text: The proposed service is specific enough for a patron to judge your usefulness.

choices.label: Promise influence beyond your standing

outcome.text: Your promise of influence reaches beyond your established position.

choices.label: Seek an introduction from a colleague

outcome.text: A colleague carries an introduction and an account of your previous work.

events.title: ANSWER A PUBLIC SCANDAL
events.text: {{rival}} has added a verse about you to a public performance. {{client}} offers a stage, with no guarantee that powerful listeners will laugh.

choices.label: Use facts and keep the verse measured

outcome.text: The verse stays close to facts that can be defended after the laughter.

choices.label: Name the powerful subject openly

outcome.text: Your public verse names the powerful subject and places your safety beside the rhyme.

choices.label: Test the verse with a fellow performer

outcome.text: A fellow performer tests the verse before it reaches the public stage.

events.title: DEFEND A TENANT
events.text: {{client}} needs evidence prepared for a proper hearing. An advocate’s opinion cannot erase a charge or end a lawful sentence.

choices.label: Prepare the real evidence for a hearing

outcome.text: Your evidence bundle is submitted for the hearing; the court retains judgment.

choices.label: Challenge the prosecution publicly

outcome.text: You publicly dispute the prosecution’s account without claiming a pardon.

choices.label: Retain a second advocate

outcome.text: A second advocate reviews the evidence and lawful grounds for defence.

events.title: INVESTIGATE A CHARTER
events.text: {{client}} produces an ancient charter whose youngest witness is inconveniently still alive. The ink and testimony need checking.

choices.label: Check the charter against witnesses

outcome.text: The charter is checked against its witnesses and surviving copies.

choices.label: Accuse the claimant of forgery now

outcome.text: You accuse the claimant openly before every disputed mark is explained.

choices.label: Commission a second reading

outcome.text: A second reader compares the ink, names and boundaries.

events.title: HEAR A SWORN CASE
events.text: {{client}} brings a sworn boundary dispute. Both neighbours claim a pig which appears to prefer a third household.

choices.label: Record sworn testimony for the court

outcome.text: Sworn testimony is recorded for the judge to consider.

choices.label: Deliver a forceful public opinion

outcome.text: Your public opinion enters the dispute as advice, with the actual court still responsible.

choices.label: Seek an agreed submission to the judge

outcome.text: The neighbours receive a proposal for an agreed submission to the judge.

events.title: RECRUIT AN ASSOCIATE
events.text: {{client}} proposes joining your associates. Their account includes three debts and an unusually detailed knowledge of the sheriff’s route.

choices.label: Check the associate’s account first

outcome.text: The proposed associate’s debts and account are checked before an agreement.

choices.label: Promise a large share for quick service

outcome.text: You offer a large share for quick service and take the risk of an untested promise.

choices.label: Ask a trusted associate to vouch for them

outcome.text: A trusted associate is asked to stake their reputation on the newcomer.

events.title: ORGANISE AN OPERATION
events.text: {{client}} brings a plan for a collector’s chest. The guards, escape route and division of the proceeds remain unsettled.

choices.label: Scout guards and plan an escape

outcome.text: The plan records guards, an escape route and what to do if the chest is empty.

choices.label: Strike before the guard changes

outcome.text: You bring the operation forward to exploit the present guard’s weakness.

choices.label: Divide the operation among trusted partners

outcome.text: Partners receive separate roles and a witnessed division of the expected proceeds.

events.title: INVESTIGATE AN INFORMER
events.text: {{client}} suspects an informer. {{rival}} is repeating details that only a few associates were supposed to know.

choices.label: Compare who knew each detail

outcome.text: The inquiry compares each leaked detail with the people who knew it.

choices.label: Confront the suspected informer

outcome.text: You confront the suspected informer and risk warning the real source.

choices.label: Use an associate to check the story

outcome.text: An associate quietly checks the account against a second witness.

events.title: THE RENT NOTCH
events.text: Your guardian’s tally stick has one notch too many. The bailiff has brought a sack large enough to contain your supper.

choices.label: Compare both halves

outcome.text: The split tally proves the payment. Your household keeps its grain.

choices.label: Cut away the notch

outcome.text: The fresh cut betrays you. Your fellow learner is accused of lending the knife.

choices.label: Ask the bailiff to produce his half

outcome.text: Your guardian brings both halves of the tally to the reeve. Neither can be altered without leaving a scar.

events.title: THE SEED POT
events.text: A rat has drowned in the pot of seed grain. Your cousin proposes burying the evidence in tomorrow’s bread.

choices.label: Sort the seed together

outcome.text: You save enough clean seed for a strip of field and share the credit.

choices.label: Blame your fellow learner

outcome.text: They are made to scrub the pot. They memorise your smile.

choices.label: Ask how seed should be stored

outcome.text: Your guardian shows you a dry bin with a stone lid. The lesson costs a pot, not a harvest.

events.title: LETTERS ON THE DOOR
events.text: Your guardian teaches letters on a soot-blackened door. A neighbour mistakes the alphabet for a curse.

choices.label: Read it aloud

outcome.text: The neighbour apologises to the letter B. Your guardian lets you keep the chalk.

choices.label: Say your classmate wrote it

outcome.text: The neighbour crosses himself at your classmate. Friendship grows colder.

choices.label: Ask your guardian to explain the letters

outcome.text: Your guardian reads a household name aloud. The neighbour recognises it and puts down the holy water.

events.title: THE WOOL ACCOUNT
events.text: The household owes six fleeces. A damp fleece weighs twice as much and smells like a drowned sheep.

choices.label: Dry and count them

outcome.text: The account balances before anyone reaches for a cudgel.

choices.label: Hide the damp one in a rival’s sack

outcome.text: The smell follows your rival into chapel. So does a grievance.

choices.label: Ask the wool buyer for a dry weight

outcome.text: The buyer provides a dry standard. Your guardian teaches you to record it before accepting a fleece.

events.title: THE SAINT WITH TWO ELBOWS
events.text: Your teacher asks you to copy the relic inventory. Saint Aelfric now possesses three elbows and no head.

choices.label: Check the older inventory

outcome.text: You restore one elbow to its rightful saint. Your teacher praises your care.

choices.label: Let your classmate copy the error

outcome.text: The visiting canon questions your classmate before the whole parish.

choices.label: Ask the canon to inspect the relic roll

outcome.text: The canon compares the old roll with yours. Saint Aelfric loses an elbow without further injury.

events.title: THE PSALTER PIG
events.text: A pig eats the lower half of a psalter page. Your mentor suggests that Providence has abbreviated the lesson.

choices.label: Reconstruct the passage

outcome.text: You and your classmate remember enough to rescue the psalm.

choices.label: Accuse your classmate of feeding it

outcome.text: The pig escapes punishment. Your classmate does not.

choices.label: Bring the damaged page to the priest

outcome.text: The priest borrows a second psalter. You learn how a missing passage is checked rather than invented.

events.title: THE BURIAL FEE
events.text: A widow’s husband appears twice in the burial ledger. She refuses to pay for the second funeral on sound theological grounds.

choices.label: Correct the account

outcome.text: The widow keeps her pennies. Your teacher trusts you with the ledger.

choices.label: Copy your rival’s signature beneath it

outcome.text: The widow curses your rival by name. They learn why at vespers.

choices.label: Ask the priest to cancel the duplicate burial

outcome.text: Your teacher strikes the second entry and explains why a clean correction beats a clever excuse.

events.title: THE BELL ROPE EXAMINATION
events.text: Your classmate is suspended from the bell rope, clutching the only clean lesson sheet.

choices.label: Help them down and share it

outcome.text: You both pass, though the bell announces it to three parishes.

choices.label: Read the answers while they dangle

outcome.text: Your work is excellent. Your classmate’s opinion of you is precise.

choices.label: Fetch the teacher and a ladder

outcome.text: The teacher lowers your classmate safely. The lesson resumes beneath a very quiet bell.

events.title: THE MASTER’S PERFECT HORSESHOE
events.text: Your master offers the inspector a horseshoe you saw crack beneath the hammer. Your fellow apprentice has been ordered to carry it.

choices.label: Repair it quietly

outcome.text: Your repair holds. The master’s reputation now rests on your hands.

choices.label: Blame the other apprentice

outcome.text: The master docks their supper. They keep the cracked shoe as evidence.

choices.label: Show the crack to the inspector

outcome.text: The inspector refuses the shoe. Your master accepts the rebuke rather less gracefully than the inspection fee.

events.title: THE STOLEN GUILD SEAL
events.text: A customer wants the guild seal on pewter spoons. The master’s silver sample is locked away with his drinking money.

choices.label: Demand a proper assay

outcome.text: The spoons fail the assay. Your careful work earns the inspector’s attention.

choices.label: Stamp the rival’s mark instead

outcome.text: A false mark reaches the guild court. Your rival begins collecting witnesses.

choices.label: Ask the master to order a public assay

outcome.text: Your master orders the assay in front of witnesses. You learn how a mark binds the maker to the metal.

events.title: THE APPRENTICE’S FINGER
events.text: A younger apprentice traps a finger in the vice. The commission is due before the bells.

choices.label: Stop work and free them

outcome.text: The apprentice keeps the finger and helps finish your commission.

choices.label: Tell the master your rival tightened it

outcome.text: The vice is opened. Your rival’s prospects close a little.

choices.label: Call the master to open the vice

outcome.text: The master stops the job and releases the apprentice. You lose an hour and learn why a commission has no fingers.

events.title: THE MASTERPIECE IN THE ASHES
events.text: A spark lands on your measured drawing. Your rival’s drawing is excellent, and unattended.

choices.label: Rebuild the measurements

outcome.text: Your teacher tests every line. The work is slow and yours.

choices.label: Present the rival’s drawing

outcome.text: The compass holes match their old work. Your mentor is less foolish than you hoped.

choices.label: Ask the master to check your surviving measurements

outcome.text: The master helps reconstruct the burnt drawing. Each borrowed measurement is acknowledged in the margin.

events.title: THE DEVIL IN THE MARGIN
events.text: Your classmate draws a bishop being swallowed by a snail. The dean calls for the artist.

choices.label: Defend it as a moral warning

outcome.text: The dean accepts a sermon on vanity. Your classmate owes you a kindness.

choices.label: Name your rival instead

outcome.text: Your rival scrapes parchment for a week and starts a private list of sins.

choices.label: Ask the dean what the snail signifies

outcome.text: The dean invents an allegory with astonishing speed. Your mentor explains which parts can safely be repeated.

events.title: THE GREEK THAT WASN’T
events.text: Your mentor’s prized Greek quotation is a laundry account in a merchant’s cipher.

choices.label: Translate it privately

outcome.text: The master changes his lecture. You receive access to a better manuscript.

choices.label: Let your rival recite it

outcome.text: The chapter learns the price of washing six shirts. Your rival learns betrayal.

choices.label: Show the quotation to your teacher in private

outcome.text: Your teacher replaces the quotation before the lecture. You receive a lesson in translating before pontificating.

events.title: THE FASTING DISPUTATION
events.text: The chapter argues whether a goose is a fish while the cook holds the knife.

choices.label: Argue from the text

outcome.text: Your argument saves the goose until supper. Your teacher respects the scholarship.

choices.label: Attribute the heresy to your rival

outcome.text: Your rival must defend a goose they have never met.

choices.label: Ask the cook to suspend judgement

outcome.text: The cook postpones the knife while your mentor checks the authorities. Theology briefly becomes useful to a goose.

events.title: THE MEDICAL GLOSS
events.text: A manuscript recommends bloodletting after a faint. Your classmate has fainted directly beneath it.

choices.label: Compare the herbal commentary

outcome.text: You keep the lancet shut and fetch water. Your classmate recovers.

choices.label: Forge the rival’s endorsement

outcome.text: The mentor catches the forged hand before the lancet opens. The grudge remains real.

choices.label: Fetch the infirmarer before the lancet

outcome.text: The infirmarer orders water and rest. Your teacher makes you record the observation beside the disputed gloss.

events.title: THE PAGE AND THE PRIVY
events.text: Your first watch is outside the lord’s privy. A visitor insists the password is a matter of terrible urgency.

choices.label: Fetch the watch sergeant

outcome.text: The visitor is admitted under escort. The sergeant trusts your judgement.

choices.label: Send your rival to stop him

outcome.text: Your rival receives the chamber pot and the blame.

choices.label: Ask the sergeant to take the watch

outcome.text: The sergeant handles the visitor and explains when urgency is an excuse and when it is a medical fact.

events.title: THE SQUIRE’S WOODEN HORSE
events.text: Your classmate’s practice saddle slips. The master calls this an opportunity to demonstrate courage.

choices.label: Secure the girth first

outcome.text: Your classmate lands upright and later returns the favour.

choices.label: Loosen the rival’s girth

outcome.text: The fall is noticed. So are your hands on the buckle.

choices.label: Ask the riding master to inspect the saddle

outcome.text: The master repairs the girth. You are made to inspect every buckle before the next ride.

events.title: THE BLUNT LANCE
events.text: The training lance bears a fresh split. The armourer offers to paint over it before the inspection.

choices.label: Replace the shaft

outcome.text: You lose an afternoon and save a face. Your master credits the inspection.

choices.label: Put it in your rival’s rack

outcome.text: The shaft breaks in their hands. They remember who visited the rack.

choices.label: Bring the shaft to the armourer

outcome.text: The armourer replaces the split wood and teaches you where a painted crack will still show under pressure.

events.title: THE HUNGRY MUSTER
events.text: The muster roll includes four dead soldiers and a horse listed as a cousin.

choices.label: Recount the living

outcome.text: Rations reach the actual company. Your teacher praises useful arithmetic.

choices.label: Sign your rival’s name to it

outcome.text: Your rival answers to the captain for a horse’s family tree.

choices.label: Ask the quartermaster to recount the roll

outcome.text: The quartermaster removes four ghosts and one horse. Your tutor makes you copy the corrected ration order.

events.title: THE WRONG COAT OF ARMS
events.text: Your tutor asks you to seat two cousins whose fathers died fighting over the same painted badger.

choices.label: Check the genealogy

outcome.text: You separate the cousins by three bishops. Dinner survives.

choices.label: Give your rival the seating plan

outcome.text: They face two angry households. Your tutor identifies the handwriting.

choices.label: Ask the herald to verify the disputed arms

outcome.text: The herald seats both cousins far from sharp cutlery. Your tutor explains the disputed descent.

events.title: THE ACCOUNT OF THE SWANS
events.text: The steward counts twelve swans. The kitchen accounts for thirteen swan pies.

choices.label: Trace the kitchen purchases

outcome.text: The thirteenth bird was a goose. Your tutor commends the audit.

choices.label: Charge the missing bird to your rival

outcome.text: The steward demands payment. Your rival begins auditing you.

choices.label: Ask the steward to reconcile the kitchen roll

outcome.text: The steward finds the goose receipt. You learn to audit the purchases before accusing the cook.

events.title: THE EMBASSY’S CHAIRS
events.text: An envoy’s chair is an inch lower than yours. His secretary calls it an insult to the whole coast.

choices.label: Offer equal stools

outcome.text: Everyone suffers equally. Your tutor calls this diplomacy.

choices.label: Say your rival ordered the chairs

outcome.text: The envoy records your rival’s name beside the word grievance.

choices.label: Ask the chamberlain to change every seat

outcome.text: The chamberlain replaces the chairs. Your tutor notes that equal discomfort is a workable diplomatic settlement.

events.title: THE TENANT’S PETITION
events.text: A tenant petitions for seed. Your tutor says this is an exercise in household administration. The tenant says he is an exercise in starvation.

choices.label: Check the granary and draft relief

outcome.text: The lesson becomes a workable petition. Your classmate helps calculate it.

choices.label: Forge your rival’s refusal

outcome.text: The tenant curses your rival. Your tutor catches the borrowed seal.

choices.label: Ask the tutor to examine the seed petition

outcome.text: Your tutor measures the household’s need against the stores. The petitioner receives an answer based on grain rather than manners.

events.title: THE WINTER ACCOUNT
events.text: {{mentor}} brings your household ledger. Winter grain and a creditor fall due together.

choices.label: Plan the stores with {{classmate}}

outcome.text: The plan protects seed and supper.

choices.label: Hide the arrears in the seed account

outcome.text: Your colleague finds the missing debt beside their signature.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to review the winter stores

outcome.text: Your tutor separates the seed reserve from the debt payment and sets a practical accounting exercise.

events.title: AN EVENING OF LETTERS
events.text: After work, {{classmate}} asks you to read a tenancy clause neither of you understood as children.

choices.label: Read it against the old agreement

outcome.text: Your shared study finds the changed rent.

choices.label: Pretend the clause favours you

outcome.text: Your colleague carries your interpretation to the landlord.

choices.label: Read the disputed tenancy clause with {{mentor}}

outcome.text: Your tutor compares both agreements and asks you to explain each changed obligation.

events.title: THE LATE READER
events.text: {{mentor}} reserves an evening for adults learning their letters. {{classmate}} brings a contract rather than a psalter.

choices.label: Read the contract together

outcome.text: You separate the obligations from the ornament.

choices.label: Copy a fluent reader’s exercise

outcome.text: The copied hand wins praise that belongs to someone else.

choices.label: Ask for an evening reading exercise

outcome.text: Your teacher sets a short contract passage that can be studied after paid work.

events.title: A LETTER HOME
events.text: {{classmate}} needs a letter to a relative who has left for work. The parish desk is finally quiet.

choices.label: Help compose an honest letter

outcome.text: Your colleague entrusts you with the reply.

choices.label: Read the private lines aloud for a laugh

outcome.text: The laughter travels; so does the betrayal.

choices.label: Ask how to write a private reply

outcome.text: Your teacher helps form a respectful letter while preserving your colleague’s confidence.

events.title: THE LATE APPRENTICE
events.text: An older apprentice is assigned the heaviest work. {{mentor}} asks whether your previous experience changes the arrangement.

choices.label: Propose a trial piece and fair rotation

outcome.text: Your work earns an adult place at the bench.

choices.label: Claim {{classmate}} made the flawed trial piece

outcome.text: The commission carries an innocent maker’s mark.

choices.label: Ask for an assessment of your previous craft work

outcome.text: Your master tests your existing skills and records what the late apprenticeship still requires.

events.title: THE EVENING MASTERPIECE
events.text: Your paying work leaves one evening to finish the apprenticeship sample. {{classmate}} offers measurements.

choices.label: Credit their help and submit your own work

outcome.text: The master tests the work and acknowledges both hands.

choices.label: Submit their sample under your mark

outcome.text: Your colleague keeps the original drawing.

choices.label: Show {{mentor}} your unfinished masterpiece

outcome.text: The master checks the surviving measurements and sets a smaller, honest trial piece.

events.title: THE INFERMARER’S COMMENTARY
events.text: {{mentor}} asks your adult seminar to compare a fever diary with an old authority. The patient’s actual course contradicts the gloss.

choices.label: Record the observations honestly

outcome.text: The seminar adopts a more careful account of care.

choices.label: Alter the diary to flatter the authority

outcome.text: Your colleague retains the unaltered observations.

choices.label: Compare the fever diary with {{mentor}}

outcome.text: Your teacher asks you to distinguish an observed symptom from an authority’s assumption.

events.title: THE VISITING EXAMINER
events.text: A visiting examiner asks how your learning was acquired while you worked. {{mentor}} can certify the hours actually completed.

choices.label: Submit the honest record

outcome.text: Your remaining requirements are written clearly.

choices.label: Borrow a completed clerical certificate

outcome.text: The borrowed certificate passes today. A later review may compare the signatures.

choices.label: Ask for the actual examination requirements

outcome.text: The examiner writes down the hours and arguments still required for a legitimate certificate.

events.title: THE VETERAN AT DRILL
events.text: {{classmate}} has seen a siege; you are learning formations after years in another trade. {{mentor}} asks for a plan.

choices.label: Combine practical experience with the drill

outcome.text: The exercise gives both adult learners useful work.

choices.label: Claim their campaign experience as yours

outcome.text: The sergeant begins asking which company remembers you.

choices.label: Review the drill with the veteran and {{mentor}}

outcome.text: Your trainer sets an exercise that tests the veteran’s experience and your understanding together.

events.title: THE CONTRACTED WATCH
events.text: Your training company must cover a night watch while keeping time for its adult recruits’ paid work.

choices.label: Draw a fair rotation

outcome.text: The company trusts the rota because you serve it too.

choices.label: Put your colleague on every cold watch

outcome.text: The rota is copied, along with its author’s name.

choices.label: Ask the captain to review the watch rotation

outcome.text: The captain checks the recruits’ paid work and makes you explain a fair allocation of cold watches.

events.title: THE PRIVATE TUTOR’S TABLE
events.text: {{mentor}} teaches court practice to adults. {{classmate}} brings a petition from their own household.

choices.label: Draft advice from the actual accounts

outcome.text: Your tutor commends a useful answer rather than a fine bow.

choices.label: Trade their private grievance for influence

outcome.text: The petition returns to its author with your name attached.

choices.label: Ask {{mentor}} to examine the household petition

outcome.text: The tutor checks the figures and asks you to justify each proposed relief payment.

events.title: THE ADULT AUDIENCE
events.text: An envoy questions why your household can afford tutoring while tenants petition for seed.

choices.label: Explain the accounts and propose affordable relief

outcome.text: Your reasoning survives questions from your colleague.

choices.label: Produce a borrowed court certificate

outcome.text: The document opens a door. The seal may be checked later.

choices.label: Ask for a witnessed court examination

outcome.text: Your tutor offers a legitimate assessment instead of a borrowed seal; the remaining preparation is recorded.

events.title: THE EVE OF BATTLE
events.text: Dawn. The enemy host gathers across the muddy field. Your sergeant bellows the order to form ranks. Your hands will not stop shaking.

choices.label: Hold the line bravely

outcome.text: You locked shields with the men beside you and held. The first charge breaks against your wall of spears.

choices.label: Pray for deliverance

outcome.text: You prayed harder than you have ever prayed. Whether God listened, the battle will decide.

choices.label: Slip toward the baggage train

outcome.text: You edged away from the front toward the wagons. Safer, until somebody notices, and then a great deal worse.

events.title: THE ROUT
events.text: The lines dissolve into screaming chaos. A mounted knight in enemy colours bears down on you, lance lowered. There is no time to think.

choices.label: Stand and brace your spear

success.text: You set your spear and the charging horse impaled itself. You stand, blood-soaked and alive, a hero of the field. The lord himself learns your name.

failure.text: The lance took you in the shoulder and the world went white. You wake days later in a surgeon’s tent, ruined but breathing.

choices.label: Dive into the mud and play dead

success.text: You lay among the fallen, unmoving, until the horses thundered past. Survival has no honour, but it has a pulse.

failure.text: A looter found you "dead" and was most surprised when you flinched. The scuffle did not go your way.

effects.death: Cut down by a battlefield looter while feigning death.

choices.label: Surrender and beg ransom

outcome.text: As a knight, you are worth more alive. You yield your sword and are held for ransom, which is humiliating and survivable, in that order.

events.title: A YEAR OF MARRIED LIFE
events.text: A year wed. The first flush has settled into something steadier. Your spouse asks, gently, what you both should build toward.

choices.label: A houseful of children

outcome.text: You agree to fill the cottage with noise and turnip-stained little hands. Terrifying. Wonderful.

choices.label: Saving toward a better life

outcome.text: You both resolve to scrimp and climb. Every coin saved is a brick in a grander future.

choices.label: Admit you are restless

outcome.text: You confess a wandering heart. The conversation is hard, and honest, and leaves a small crack that may yet widen.

events.title: THE RIVAL · A CONTEST MADE PUBLIC
events.text: someone once known in Swineford challenges you to carry a sack of turnips across the village green. They have drawn a finish line, gathered a crowd and already practised their victory bow.

choices.label: Win the turnip race

outcome.text: You cross first, wheezing turnip dust. {{rival.name}} insists the sack was uneven. The crowd insists they do the victory bow anyway.

choices.label: Refuse to make it a contest

outcome.text: You ask why anyone should carry turnips for free. The crowd drifts away. {{rival.name}} is left guarding two sacks and an excellent bow.

choices.label: Try to make an ally of them instead

outcome.text: You offer to carry the sack together. {{rival.name}} accuses you of pitying them, then drops it on their own foot.

events.title: THE RIVAL · A PATRON TAKES AN INTEREST
events.text: someone once known in Swineford has hired someone once known in Swineford to supervise the prize pigs. Your rival struts through the market wearing a brass badge that says Deputy Pig Marshal. They tell you the job comes with paid meals.

choices.label: Put yourself in front of {{patron.name}} too

outcome.text: You offer to keep the pig accounts. {{patron.name}} likes your confidence. {{rival.name}} now has to explain every missing turnip to you.

choices.label: Improve your own vegetable patch

outcome.text: You improve your own vegetable patch and fill the store cupboard. No patron required. No badge either, which is a mercy.

choices.label: Let {{patron.name}} hear the worst of them

outcome.text: You tell {{patron.name}} that the Deputy Pig Marshal lost a pig inside the chapel. It is true. Repeating the part about the baptismal font is optional, but you do.

events.title: THE RIVAL · A RUMOUR WITH ONE SOURCE
events.text: someone once known in Swineford claims you stole the church bell’s clapper and sold it as a soup ladle. Three market sellers repeat the story. Customers are starting to avoid your household.

choices.label: Name {{rival.name}} as the source, publicly

outcome.text: You name {{rival.name}} as the liar and demand they produce the alleged ladle. Half the market cheers. The other half wants to see the ladle.

choices.label: Trace it properly and say nothing yet

outcome.text: You question the sellers. Each heard the tale from {{rival.name}}, who received a sealed note from {{patron.name}}. You keep the note.

choices.label: Make sure it cannot touch your household

outcome.text: You settle your household’s accounts in front of witnesses. The traders keep selling to your family, though the ladle jokes continue.

events.title: THE RIVAL · BEFORE THE WHOLE HALL
events.text: At the village hall, someone once known in Swineford repeats the bell-clapper accusation before someone once known in Swineford. The priest arrives carrying the actual clapper. He would like everyone to stop discussing his ladle.

choices.label: Offer them terms in front of everyone

outcome.text: You offer a truce: no more rumours, no pressure on either household, and one public apology each. {{rival.name}} agrees. The priest takes his clapper home.

choices.label: Make them repeat the accusation beside the evidence

outcome.text: You ask the priest to hold up the clapper while {{rival.name}} repeats the accusation. They cannot finish. You have won, and made the humiliation needlessly thorough.

choices.label: Decline to answer and leave the hall

outcome.text: You leave the hall to finish your household’s accounts. The crowd calls it surrender. Your family calls it finally being home for supper.

events.title: THE RIVAL · THE FEUD IN DAYLIGHT
events.text: The market is arguing over the missing clapper. someone once known in Swineford demands an apology. someone once known in Swineford offers to settle the quarrel if you both work for lower wages.

choices.label: Press it while you have the advantage

outcome.text: You ask {{rival.name}} to describe the ladle. They change its size three times. The crowd laughs, then gets tired of you asking a fourth time.

choices.label: Say your piece once and then stop

outcome.text: You point out that the church bell still rings. Then you stop talking. The bell supplies a considerably better argument.

events.title: THE RIVAL · THE SHAPE OF THE THING
events.text: The sealed note proves someone once known in Swineford invented the clapper story. A second note offers both of you lower wages while your reputations recover. Your patron is paying you less to clean up their own lie.

choices.label: Use what you have found

outcome.text: You send both notes to the guild clerk. The wage-cut scheme collapses. {{rival.name}} blames you for exposing how easily they were fooled.

choices.label: Show {{rival.name}} what you found

outcome.text: You show {{rival.name}} both notes. They read the wage offer twice, then call {{patron.name}} a name usually reserved for diseased turnips.

events.title: THE RIVAL · IT COMES TO THE DOOR ANYWAY
events.text: someone once known in Swineford tells the miller to refuse your household’s grain. The miller asks you to settle the feud before everyone has to eat turnip soup.

choices.label: Tell them the household is out of it

outcome.text: You tell {{rival.name}} to bring complaints to you, not the miller. They agree to leave your household alone and immediately insult you instead.

choices.label: Go after theirs

outcome.text: You persuade a baker to refuse their household’s flour. Now two innocent families need supper and both shopkeepers regret knowing you.

events.title: THE RIVAL · TWO LIVES MEASURED AGAINST EACH OTHER
events.text: someone once known in Swineford meets you at market without an insult prepared. You discuss turnip prices. It is an unexpectedly pleasant improvement.

choices.label: Let it be finished

outcome.text: You and {{rival.name}} jointly challenge a trader’s false weights. The trader looks at both of you and quietly fetches the honest scales.

memory.note: The rivalry ended with public apologies and a promise to leave both households alone.

events.title: THE RIVAL · WHAT THE RIVALRY MADE
events.text: You and someone once known in Swineford pass on opposite sides of the market. The bell rings overhead. Neither of you mentions kitchen utensils.

choices.label: Take what it made of you

outcome.text: You keep your accounts precise and your accusations provable. Your family has learned the same lesson, at the cost of many uncomfortable dinners.

events.title: THE LEAN HARVEST · THE PRICE MOVES BEFORE THE BELL STOPS
events.text: The corn comes in sparse and damp. someone once known in Swineford has raised the price of a bushel before the church bell has finished ringing the news.

choices.label: Buy at the new price at once (10g)

outcome.text: Ten shillings for grain that was eight yesterday. It is a bad price and it is the best price anybody in Swineford gets for the next twelve months.

choices.label: Demand the assize price be enforced

outcome.text: You cite the assize at the reeve in front of the market. He agrees, reluctantly, and {{merchant.name}} sells at the lawful price and remembers who made him.

choices.label: Wait and see if it settles

outcome.text: It does not settle. By Martinmas it is fourteen and by Candlemas there is none at any price.

events.title: THE LEAN HARVEST · WHAT {{reeve.name}} SAYS ABOUT THE STORES
events.text: Households are missing meals and someone once known in Swineford keeps saying the common stores are being managed fairly. Nobody has seen inside the store since Michaelmas.

choices.label: Demand the store be counted in front of witnesses

outcome.text: Six men, a tally and an afternoon. It is being managed fairly, actually, and there is a great deal less of it than anybody had assumed.

choices.label: Feed the worst-off out of your own stores

outcome.text: You do it without announcing it, which means five households eat and the rest of the lane assumes nobody did anything.

choices.label: Back {{reeve.name}} in public

outcome.text: You say the stores are being managed properly. It is true, and it buys the parish four weeks of calm that nobody has earned.

events.title: THE LEAN HARVEST · A STOREHOUSE BROKEN IN THE NIGHT
events.text: The store is broken open and emptied. Hungry neighbours are looking at the ground, someone once known in Swineford is demanding hangings, and how this is answered decides how the winter goes.

choices.label: Open the remaining stores yourself, publicly

outcome.text: You open the doors and distribute in daylight before anybody can stop you. It is theft with better manners and it is entirely defensible to everybody who is hungry.

choices.label: Audit every sack and every price first

outcome.text: Three weeks of tallies. You establish exactly how much grain exists in Swineford and exactly who is sitting on it, and both numbers surprise everybody.

choices.label: Secure your own household’s grain first

outcome.text: You move your stores somewhere defensible and put a man on them. Your household eats all winter and is watched doing it.

events.title: THE LEAN HARVEST · THE CROWD AT {{reeve.name}}’S DOOR
events.text: A crowd is outside someone once known in Swineford’s door with empty sacks and farm tools. It is not yet a riot and it will be within the hour, and you are the only person both sides will listen to.

choices.label: Get both sides to agree a distribution on the spot

outcome.text: Forty minutes on a doorstep and a written agreement about weekly measures. Nobody gets what they came for and nobody is hanged for it either.

choices.label: Send for the lord’s men

outcome.text: Seventeen armed retainers and the crowd is off the lane in twenty minutes. Four men are amerced, one is gaoled, and the winter passes very quietly indeed.

choices.label: Go home and bar the door

outcome.text: You are not there. It goes the way it goes, {{reeve.name}}’s door comes off its hinges, and nobody ever asks where you were because everybody knows.

events.title: THE LEAN HARVEST · THE GRANARY OPEN AND THE CROWD IN IT
events.text: The doors are open and the distribution has become a crush. Generosity has turned into a problem of order within about ninety seconds.

choices.label: Impose a list and a queue

outcome.text: You get a list of households, a rota and two large men on the door. It is slower, it is fairer, and nobody is trampled.

choices.label: Let it run

outcome.text: It empties in an afternoon. The strongest households carry off most of it and two of the weakest go home with an empty sack, which is precisely backwards.

events.title: THE LEAN HARVEST · FALSE WEIGHTS AND A HIDDEN STORE
events.text: The tallies produce two facts: someone once known in Swineford’s bushel is light, and there are forty quarters of sound grain in a barn that is not on anybody’s list.

choices.label: Read both facts out at the hallmote

outcome.text: The measure is broken in front of the market and the barn is opened by order. It is complete, it is public, and it makes an enemy with money.

choices.label: Put both facts to {{merchant.name}} privately

outcome.text: He sells the forty quarters into Swineford at the assize price by the end of the week and nobody ever learns why. He hates you accurately and permanently.

events.title: THE LEAN HARVEST · SMOKE FROM YOUR CHIMNEY
events.text: Your household eats. The lane can see the smoke from your oven every morning and has begun to have opinions about it out loud.

choices.label: Start baking for four other households

outcome.text: Your oven, their flour where they have any and yours where they do not. It costs a third of your stores and it ends the conversation in the lane.

choices.label: Bake earlier and keep the door shut

outcome.text: You move the baking to before first light. Everybody knows anyway. The lane simply stops mentioning it in front of you, and that is the part that stings.

events.title: THE LEAN HARVEST · THE BARNS FILL AGAIN
events.text: The next harvest is ordinary, which after this year passes for plenty. Swineford has a written arrangement about lean years that it did not have in the spring.

choices.label: Keep the arrangement in the parish chest

outcome.text: You put the grain-sharing rules in the parish chest. The clerk adds a large drawing of a sack for the councillor who pretends to read.

memory.note: Swineford came out of a famine year with a written rule for the next one.

events.title: THE LEAN HARVEST · WHO FED IT AND WHO PROFITED
events.text: The barns fill again. Swineford keeps a very exact account of who fed it, who profited from it, and who sent armed men down the lane.

choices.label: Let the account stand

outcome.text: It stands for two generations, unwritten and word-perfect. Four families are still explaining their grandparents in 1390.

events.title: THE INHERITANCE · A CLAIM AND A WITNESS
events.text: someone once known in Swineford produces a claim on family property and asks someone once known in Swineford to support it. someone once known in Swineford has not said yes and has not said no.

choices.label: Get to {{witness.name}} first

outcome.text: You reach them before the claimant does. What they actually remember is less than either side wants and more than either side feared.

choices.label: Concede the part of the claim that is sound

outcome.text: You give up a third of it immediately and publicly. It costs real land and it makes the remaining two-thirds nearly unassailable.

choices.label: Refuse the whole claim outright

outcome.text: You reject all of it in front of the family. {{claimant.name}} was expecting a negotiation and now has nothing to lose, which was not the intention.

events.title: THE INHERITANCE · A PROMISE REPEATED UNTIL IT IS LAW
events.text: A deathbed promise is being repeated at every gathering as though repetition makes it enforceable. Two people who were in the room remember it differently and both are certain.

choices.label: Have both accounts written down and sealed

outcome.text: Two statements, two seals, both preserved. Neither is proved and neither can now quietly change, which turns out to matter enormously.

choices.label: Repeat your version more often and louder

outcome.text: It works, in the sense that by spring most of the family believes it. It is exactly the tactic you objected to and everybody notices.

choices.label: Find whether anybody else was in the room

outcome.text: A servant was, and is alive, and is now the most important person in the county and knows it.

events.title: THE INHERITANCE · A CONVENIENT SEAL AND AN AWKWARD DATE
events.text: A document appears with a seal that is entirely convincing and a date that cannot possibly be right. How you handle it decides whether this stays a family matter.

choices.label: Denounce it as a forgery in open court

outcome.text: You take the date apart in front of the steward. It is devastating, it is correct, and it turns a family argument into a criminal one.

choices.label: Say nothing and find out who made it

outcome.text: The seal is genuine and fourteen years old, reused. Whoever did this had access to the family chest, and the list of those people is very short.

choices.label: Take it to the family before the court

outcome.text: You put it on the table at home and say that whoever did it should say so now. Somebody does, eventually, at about midnight.

events.title: THE INHERITANCE · JUDGMENT BEFORE THE WHOLE FAMILY
events.text: someone once known in Swineford demands a settlement in front of the family and the village. Everybody who will inherit anything from anybody is in the room watching how this is done.

choices.label: Settle for less than you could take

outcome.text: You take about two-thirds of what a court would have given you and say why, out loud, in front of everyone. Nobody is thrilled and nobody is finished.

choices.label: Take the whole of what is yours

outcome.text: You take all of it, lawfully, and the roll agrees with you completely. {{claimant.name}} is a tenant of somebody else by Michaelmas.

choices.label: Give up the claim entirely

outcome.text: You walk away from the whole thing in front of everybody. It is either the most generous or the most contemptuous act of your life and opinion is divided permanently.

events.title: THE INHERITANCE · CLAIM AGAINST CLAIM
events.text: someone once known in Swineford answers in kind: witnesses, anger, and a second document that is considerably better made than the first.

choices.label: Press for a criminal charge

outcome.text: You go for forgery rather than for the land. It is winnable and it will hang somebody in your own family if it succeeds.

choices.label: Drop the forgery and argue the land alone

outcome.text: You take the hanging off the table and argue the property on its merits. It is slower, it is smaller, and nobody in the family dies of it.

events.title: THE INHERITANCE · WHO HAD THE KEY TO THE CHEST
events.text: The list of people who could have taken that seal is four names long, and one of them is someone once known in Swineford, who has been helping you all year.

choices.label: Put it to {{witness.name}}

outcome.text: They admit it in about four seconds and explain why, and the reason is better than you wanted it to be.

choices.label: Keep {{witness.name}}’s name out of it

outcome.text: You solve the forgery in a way that never requires the fourth name. It costs you the cleanest version of your case and it is the right call.

events.title: THE INHERITANCE · A TABLE AND NO LAWYERS
events.text: The family sits down without proctors. Old affection turns out to be useful and old grievance turns out to be more detailed.

choices.label: Get a division agreed at the table tonight

outcome.text: A long evening, one very bad half-hour, and a division everybody signs before going to bed. It is uneven and it is agreed.

choices.label: Adjourn before somebody says something final

outcome.text: You stop the inheritance meeting before anyone throws the inkpot. Each claimant must bring a written proposal next time.

events.title: THE INHERITANCE · WHAT THE HEIRS ACTUALLY GET
events.text: The property is divided and the family survives the dividing. Any clerk can do the first part.

choices.label: Have the division written and witnessed

outcome.text: Sealed, witnessed, and copied three times. Not one of the next four generations has to argue about any of it, and none of them knows why.

memory.note: A disputed inheritance was divided by agreement and written down.

events.title: THE INHERITANCE · THE LAND HAS AN OWNER
events.text: The property is settled beyond appeal. The family is settled too, into two halves that will be introduced to each other at funerals for the next sixty years.

choices.label: Take possession

outcome.text: You take the whole estate. Your relatives refuse the celebratory supper and send back the invitation wrapped around a dead onion.

events.title: WAR · BANNERS ON THE CAMBRIDGE ROAD
events.text: someone once known in Swineford arrives under a war banner wanting men, carts and grain out of Swineford, and has the writ to take all three whether the village agrees or not.

choices.label: Negotiate what goes and what stays

outcome.text: You spend an evening arguing over a tally and keep back the plough oxen and the seed corn. It is the difference between a hard year and no year at all.

choices.label: Give them everything on the writ

outcome.text: Everything on the list, promptly and without argument. {{commander.name}} notes the village as cooperative and comes back in the spring for more.

choices.label: Hide half of it before they finish counting

outcome.text: Two carts of grain into the mere field overnight. It works, it feeds Swineford in March, and it is a hanging matter if the count is ever checked.

events.title: WAR · {{companion.name}} ASKS WHETHER YOU ARE COMING
events.text: someone once known in Swineford is on the muster roll and asks, directly and only once, whether you will be standing next to them.

choices.label: Put your name down beside theirs

outcome.text: You write it in and they visibly stop being frightened, which is most of what they were asking for.

choices.label: Get {{companion.name}} taken off the roll instead

outcome.text: It costs six shillings and a favour and it works. They are furious about it for a year and alive for forty.

choices.label: Tell them plainly that you are not coming

outcome.text: You say it to their face rather than letting them find out at the muster. It is the smallest possible decency and it is the one they remember.

events.title: WAR · THE COLLECTORS EMPTY THE BARNS
events.text: Purveyors are taking what the writ did not cover and paying in tallies redeemable at the Exchequer, eventually, in theory. What you do about it sets Swineford’s war.

choices.label: Answer the muster yourself and go with the carts

outcome.text: If Swineford’s grain is going, you go with it, and a surprising amount of it arrives where it is supposed to because you are standing next to it.

choices.label: Fortify the village and find out where the war is

outcome.text: A ditch, a bank, two watchmen and a boy on a fast pony. You know where the fighting is four days before anybody else in the hundred.

choices.label: Move your household off the line of march

outcome.text: Four miles to kin, with the beasts, before the second column comes through. It is the correct decision and Swineford watches you make it.

events.title: WAR · SMOKE ON THE SWINEFORD HORIZON
events.text: It has come to the village itself. someone once known in Swineford must hold the road or give up Swineford, and is genuinely asking rather than telling.

choices.label: Pay the fine and open the road

outcome.text: Forty marks raised in a day and the column takes it and goes past. Swineford is poor for a decade and standing, and two men call you a coward at the ale for years.

choices.label: Hold the road

outcome.text: It is held. Nineteen dead, the mill burned, the column turned, and a story that is told in that village for two hundred years with your name in it.

choices.label: Get everybody out and give them the village

outcome.text: Swineford empties in six hours. The column takes an empty village, burns half of it out of irritation, and nobody at all is killed.

events.title: WAR · BENEATH THE BANNER
events.text: You are standing with someone once known in Swineford while someone once known in Swineford arranges a defence that depends on the left holding for rather longer than the left can hold.

choices.label: Tell {{commander.name}} the left will not hold

outcome.text: You say it in front of his officers and you are right. He changes the disposition, resents you for the rest of the campaign, and loses sixteen men instead of ninety.

choices.label: Ask to be put on the left

outcome.text: You go where it is going to break. It breaks anyway and rather later than it would have, and you are carried off it.

events.title: WAR · DITCH, BANK AND A BOY ON A PONY
events.text: The scouts come back: the enemy column is taking the ford road, not the Cambridge road, and will be at Swineford in two days rather than never.

choices.label: Break the ford causeway

outcome.text: A morning with mattocks and the ford is impassable to carts. The column goes round by nine miles and Swineford is not on its road at all.

choices.label: Send the boy on to warn the next four villages

outcome.text: You give up your only fast rider and your two days of advantage. Four villages get out in time and Swineford meets the column with no warning of its own.

events.title: WAR · THE ROAD FULL OF PEOPLE
events.text: You are six miles off with the household intact and the road behind you is filling with people from Swineford who left it later than you did.

choices.label: Take in whoever reaches you

outcome.text: Nineteen people in a barn meant for four and every scrap of food gone in twenty days. Not one of them is turned away and not one of them forgets it.

choices.label: Go further

outcome.text: Another ten miles to a place with no war in it. Your household is entirely safe and entirely absent, and both facts are noted at home.

events.title: WAR · THE BANNERS GO PAST
events.text: The war moves on somewhere else. Swineford has its people, most of its roofs, and a debt it will be paying at every Michaelmas for five years.

choices.label: Start paying it

outcome.text: The village pays it off in 1361 and holds an ale for the occasion. Nobody at the ale is entirely sure any more whether it was the right decision.

memory.note: Swineford bought its way out of a battle and paid for it for six years.

events.title: WAR · THE RETURNING BANNERS
events.text: The survivors come back different. Swineford counts nineteen graves, one burned mill and a set of reputations that will not be adjusted again in anybody’s lifetime.

choices.label: Count them properly

outcome.text: Every name on a board in the church, in order, including the two that somebody wanted left off. It is there in 1500 and the paint has been renewed four times.

events.title: THE AMBITIOUS CHILD · MORE THAN THE HOUSE CAN GIVE
events.text: someone once known in Swineford tells you what they want, and it is bigger than this household, this village and anything either of your parents attempted.

choices.label: Tell them to go after it

outcome.text: You say it plainly and immediately. They are so unprepared for it that they cry, which neither of you mentions ever again.

choices.label: Ask them how, specifically

outcome.text: You make them account for every step of it. Two of the steps do not exist, they find that out from you rather than from the world, and they go and fix them.

choices.label: Remind them what the holding needs

outcome.text: It is true, it is necessary, and it is what your own father said to you, in nearly the same words, which occurs to you about a week later.

events.title: THE AMBITIOUS CHILD · {{mentor.name}} OFFERS TO HELP
events.text: someone once known in Swineford offers to take someone once known in Swineford on. The offer is generous, the terms are vague, and nothing in Swineford has ever been free.

choices.label: Get the terms in writing before anything else

outcome.text: Three evenings and an indenture that specifies keep, years, and what happens if either side wants out. {{mentor.name}} is mildly offended and signs.

choices.label: Take the offer as given

outcome.text: A handshake and goodwill. It works until the third summer, when there is a disagreement about what was meant and nothing to point at.

choices.label: Find out what {{mentor.name}} wants first

outcome.text: They want a connection to your household in about seven years for reasons they will not state. It is not sinister and it is not nothing.

events.title: THE AMBITIOUS CHILD · THE OTHER CHILDREN ARE COUNTING
events.text: What has gone to someone once known in Swineford in coin, time and attention has been noticed by the rest of the household and is being tallied with some accuracy.

choices.label: Back {{child.name}} openly and say the rest must wait

outcome.text: You say it out loud at the table: this one, now, and the others when it comes back. It is honest, it is a gamble, and everybody knows exactly where they stand.

choices.label: Set conditions and test {{mentor.name}} properly

outcome.text: Progress reviewed each Michaelmas, money released against results. {{child.name}} finds it humiliating and it saves them from two very bad decisions.

choices.label: Balance it, and give something to every child

outcome.text: You divide what there is between all of them. Nobody is neglected, nothing is enough for anything, and {{child.name}} watches the chance go.

events.title: THE AMBITIOUS CHILD · CHILD AGAINST PARENT
events.text: someone once known in Swineford refuses the future you chose and demands to name their own, in front of the household, without leaving either of you a graceful exit.

choices.label: Give way, and say why you were wrong

outcome.text: You admit that you mistook your child’s independence for ingratitude. The room goes quiet. Your child takes your hand.

choices.label: Refuse, and make it stick

outcome.text: You hold, entirely, and you have the household and the holding to hold with. They comply. They are still complying at forty and you can see it.

choices.label: Tell them it is theirs to decide and step out of it

outcome.text: You take yourself out of the decision entirely and mean it. They are free, unadvised, and rather more frightened than they expected to be.

events.title: THE AMBITIOUS CHILD · A DOOR THROWN OPEN
events.text: someone once known in Swineford takes the chance and is immediately very good at it, which attracts admiration, envy and a set of expectations nobody has warned them about.

choices.label: Warn them what the envy will cost

outcome.text: You tell them what to expect from people who have known them since they were small. They do not believe you until Lammas and then they do.

choices.label: Stay out of the way

outcome.text: You let them run at it without commentary. They go faster and further and hit the first wall entirely unprepared.

events.title: THE AMBITIOUS CHILD · THE MENTOR UNDER TERMS
events.text: someone once known in Swineford accepts every condition without argument, which is either good faith or the behaviour of somebody with a longer plan. someone once known in Swineford resents every review.

choices.label: Hold to the terms exactly

outcome.text: You inspect the accounts at the agreed review. A landlord has charged rent twice. You catch the duplicate before your child pays it.

choices.label: Ease the conditions as they prove themselves

outcome.text: You loosen it year by year as they earn it. It is what they needed, and it takes away the one thing that was catching their mistakes.

events.title: THE AMBITIOUS CHILD · WATCHING IT GO
events.text: The household is steady, fair and unremarkable. someone once known in Swineford can see the chance receding at a measurable rate and has stopped mentioning it.

choices.label: Find them a smaller chance you can actually afford

outcome.text: Not the thing they wanted. A real thing, within reach, that you can pay for. They take it and are quietly furious and quietly successful.

choices.label: Let it go

outcome.text: The chance passes and nothing is said. They are a competent, unremarkable adult who is very good to their siblings and never once raises it.

events.title: THE AMBITIOUS CHILD · THE PERSON THEY BECAME
events.text: They are grown and they are theirs, and they come back on their own account rather than because they were told to.

choices.label: Meet them as an equal

outcome.text: They visit twice a year for the rest of your life and argue with you as an equal, loudly, over supper, about nothing much.

memory.note: A child you gave way to became someone who chose to come back.

events.title: THE AMBITIOUS CHILD · WHAT THE UPBRINGING MADE
events.text: They are grown, capable, dutiful and entirely closed. The holding is in good hands and there is a conversation the two of you have never had and now will not.

choices.label: Hand over the holding

outcome.text: They take it, run it better than you did, and are unfailingly correct with you until the end. Nobody outside the household ever notices anything wrong.

events.title: THE COMMON ROUND · THE BOON-WORK FALLS IN THE RAIN
events.text: someone once known in Swineford brings word that the lord’s boon-work has been called for the three driest days of the month, which are the three days every holding in Swineford needs for its own hay.

choices.label: Get the village to ask for a different week

outcome.text: Thirteen households put the same request in the same words at the same hallmote. The steward moves it, grumbling, and notes that Swineford is organised.

choices.label: Cut your own hay at night and do the boon-work anyway

outcome.text: Three nights by moonlight and three days on the lord’s meadow. Your hay is in, you are half dead, and you owe nobody anything.

events.title: THE COMMON ROUND · THE HAYWARD TAKES AGAINST A HOUSEHOLD
events.text: The hayward has presented one household five times this year for things everybody does. someone once known in Swineford says it is because of an old argument over a gate.

choices.label: Get the presentments read out together

outcome.text: Five presentments against one household and none against anybody else, read one after another. The steward sees it instantly and the hayward is replaced at Michaelmas.

choices.label: Pay their amercements and keep out of it

outcome.text: Fourpence four times. The household is grateful, the hayward is undisturbed, and you have solved this year and not the next one.

events.title: THE COMMON ROUND · THE STEWARD WANTS A REEVE
events.text: The manor needs a reeve for the year: unpaid, unpopular, responsible for everybody else’s arrears, and excused their own rent. someone once known in Swineford says the village would elect you if you let them.

choices.label: Take it

outcome.text: A year of collecting from neighbours and answering to a steward. You are rent-free and nobody in Swineford quite talks to you the same way again.

choices.label: Refuse and let it fall on somebody else

outcome.text: It falls on a man who cannot say no and cannot do the arithmetic, and the whole village pays for that by Michaelmas.

events.title: THE COMMON ROUND · THE ARREARS OF A NEIGHBOUR
events.text: One household is six shillings behind and cannot pay. someone once known in Swineford points out that the arrears are recoverable from the village as a whole, or from that household’s beasts, and the choice of which is being left to you.

choices.label: Spread it across the whole village

outcome.text: Elevenpence a household and a very cold reception at four doors. The family keeps its beasts and stays on its land, which was the entire point.

choices.label: Take the beasts

outcome.text: Two oxen distrained and sold. The books balance perfectly, the steward is impressed, and the household is cottars by Lady Day.

events.title: THE COMMON ROUND · THE VILLAGE THAT COVERS ITSELF
events.text: Swineford agrees to share the unpaid dues of four struggling families. The collections cover this year’s arrears and keep those households on their land.

choices.label: Let it become the custom

outcome.text: The village agrees to keep the arrangement. For now, neighbours have a custom they can call on when the harvest fails.

events.title: THE COMMON ROUND · A VERY GOOD SET OF BOOKS
events.text: Your year as reeve produces the cleanest account roll the manor has seen. The steward remembers your name and so, differently, does the lane.

choices.label: Take the steward’s notice

outcome.text: Better work follows and so does a coolness in Swineford that never entirely lifts. Both were bought with the same two oxen.

events.title: THE CONTESTED TRADE · THE ASSIZE OF BREAD AND ALE
events.text: someone once known in Swineford warns you the aletasters are coming through and that the assize price has moved since the last grain returns, downward, which nobody has told the traders.

choices.label: Price to the new assize immediately

outcome.text: You are the only stall pricing correctly on the day the tasters walk through. Four of your neighbours are amerced and every one of them knows you knew.

choices.label: Tell nobody and hold the old price for a week

outcome.text: A week of the old price and then a very quick correction the morning the tasters arrive. Eight shillings and no amercement.

events.title: THE CONTESTED TRADE · FORESTALLING ON THE ROAD
events.text: Somebody is meeting the carts a mile outside Swineford and buying the whole load before it reaches the market. It is illegal, it is profitable, and someone once known in Swineford can name him.

choices.label: Present him for forestalling

outcome.text: He is amerced and does it again by a different road within a month. The presentment costs him twopence and costs you a permanent enemy with capital.

choices.label: Meet the carts two miles out

outcome.text: You go further out than he does and buy earlier. It works beautifully and the market price in Swineford is now set entirely on the Cambridge road.

events.title: THE CONTESTED TRADE · A BAD BATCH UNDER YOUR MARK
events.text: Seven pieces have gone out under your mark with a fault in them that will show in five winters or so. someone once known in Swineford noticed before the buyers did.

choices.label: Recall all seven and replace them

outcome.text: You go to seven doors, admit it, and replace the lot at your own cost. The expense hurts, but the buyers praise your honesty and the guild takes notice.

choices.label: Say nothing and improve the next batch

outcome.text: You leave the suspect pieces in circulation and improve the next batch. Nobody has connected the faults yet; you keep the list of buyers to yourself.

events.title: THE CONTESTED TRADE · THE GUILD OFFERS YOU THE SEARCH
events.text: The wardens offer you the searchership: you inspect every shop in the trade, condemn what fails, and set the standard for the town. It is power, and it is unpaid, and it makes you responsible for other men’s livelihoods.

choices.label: Take it and search honestly

outcome.text: You condemn work belonging to two men who have fed you and one who is owed money by you. Nobody ever accuses you of favour and nobody ever thanks you either.

choices.label: Take it and search selectively

outcome.text: Your competitors are searched thoroughly and your friends are searched on a Friday afternoon. Orders move to your shop, bringing profit and uncomfortable questions.

events.title: THE CONTESTED TRADE · A MARK THAT MEANS SOMETHING
events.text: The standard holds because it was applied to everybody including you. Buyers three counties off ask for Swineford work by name, which has never happened before.

choices.label: Keep searching honestly

outcome.text: You record the faults honestly and settle the outstanding orders. Your fair dealing earns both payment and the guild’s respect.

events.title: THE CONTESTED TRADE · THE LARGEST SHOP IN THE TOWN
events.text: Yours is the biggest shop in the trade and the trade knows precisely how it got that way. Nobody says it, because you are also the searcher.

choices.label: Keep the search and the shop

outcome.text: You keep the appointment and the profit from this order. Your household grows richer, but the guild questions whose interests your inspections serve.

events.title: THE CURE OF SOULS · THE UNBAPTISED CHILD
events.text: someone once known in Swineford brings a child born in the night to a woman with no husband anybody will name. The child is weak, and the question of whether it is baptised before dawn is not a theological one tonight.

choices.label: Baptise it at once and ask nothing

outcome.text: Done before first light with two women as witnesses. The child lives. The question of the father is never entered in any book.

choices.label: Baptise it and present the mother for leyrwite

outcome.text: Both are done properly. The child is saved and the mother pays sixpence she does not have and stands up in front of the parish.

events.title: THE CURE OF SOULS · WHAT WAS SAID IN CONFESSION
events.text: Somebody has confessed something that will kill another person if it stays secret. The seal of confession is absolute and there is no version of this where you are not complicit in something.

choices.label: Work on the penitent until they tell it themselves

outcome.text: Four months of the hardest pastoral work of your life. They tell it, in the end, in their own voice, and nobody dies.

choices.label: Keep the seal absolutely

outcome.text: You keep it, entirely, as you are bound to. Somebody dies in March and you say the words over them knowing what you knew.

events.title: THE CURE OF SOULS · THE BISHOP WANTS THE PARISH SILENT
events.text: A letter comes: the parish is to stop asking about where the tithe corn goes, and to be told from the pulpit that the question is itself a sin. someone once known in Swineford has read it over your shoulder.

choices.label: Preach on stewardship instead

outcome.text: You preach a scrupulously orthodox sermon on the duties of stewards that answers the question completely without once mentioning it. The parish understands perfectly.

choices.label: Preach the letter as written

outcome.text: You say from the pulpit that asking is a sin. Fifteen people stop coming and four of them never come back to any church at all.

events.title: THE CURE OF SOULS · A PATRON’S OFFER
events.text: A wealthy church patron offers a paid commission. Taking it means less time this season for three local families in genuine trouble.

choices.label: Refuse it and stay

outcome.text: You write a short, polite refusal and put it in the fire twice before sending it. You make time for the three families and help them through the immediate trouble.

choices.label: Take it

outcome.text: You accept the commission and its payment. The patron commends your work; the three families must wait for your attention.

events.title: THE CURE OF SOULS · A PARISH THAT TRUSTS YOU
events.text: The families you helped thank you after the service. Their trust was earned through small duties that could easily have been neglected.

choices.label: Renew your commitment

outcome.text: The parish records its thanks and promises help with your work. You return to your duties with stronger support and a name people trust.

events.title: THE CURE OF SOULS · THE PATRON’S FAVOUR
events.text: The commission brings money and influence within the church. Your patron offers further support, while local families still need your time.

choices.label: Get on with the work

outcome.text: You accept the patron’s support and complete the agreed work. Your household benefits, and the demands on your attention remain.

events.title: THE SOLDIER’S ROAD · THE ARRAY IS SHORT OF ARCHERS
events.text: someone once known in Swineford says the array is six archers short and the shortfall will be made up from whoever is standing in the butts on Sunday, whether they can draw or not.

choices.label: Train them properly before the muster

outcome.text: Six weeks of Sundays and a great deal of shouting. Six men who can draw a bow instead of six men holding one.

choices.label: Get yourself named to the retinue instead

outcome.text: You are attached to a retinue rather than the array, which is better pay, better company, and considerably nearer the fighting.

events.title: THE SOLDIER’S ROAD · AN ORDER TO FIRE THE VILLAGE
events.text: The order is to burn a village on the line of march to deny it to the enemy. It is a sound military decision and there are people in it.

choices.label: Get them out first and burn it slowly

outcome.text: You lose half a day and the village burns with nobody in it. Your captain says nothing about the half day and does not forget it.

choices.label: Burn it on time

outcome.text: It is done inside the hour exactly as ordered. You are commended in front of the retinue and you are careful, afterwards, not to think about the hour.

events.title: THE SOLDIER’S ROAD · THE WAGES DO NOT COME
events.text: Eight weeks unpaid and the retinue is beginning to take payment from the countryside instead. someone once known in Swineford says it starts as requisition and it never stays requisition.

choices.label: Ride to the paymaster and refuse to leave

outcome.text: Six days in an antechamber being extremely polite. The wages arrive, eight weeks of them, and the countryside is not touched.

choices.label: Take what the retinue is owed from the country

outcome.text: Nineteen weeks of wages taken in kind from people who owe you nothing. The men are paid, the retinue holds together, and three villages remember the badge.

events.title: THE SOLDIER’S ROAD · THE CAPTAINCY AND THE GARRISON
events.text: You are offered a captaincy on a campaign that will make a name, or the command of the shire garrison, which is dull, permanent, and the only thing standing between the coast road and the villages behind it.

choices.label: Take the garrison

outcome.text: You organise patrols, drills and watch rotations. Merchants report a quieter road, and the nearby villages welcome the extra protection.

choices.label: Take the captaincy

outcome.text: You lead a hard-fought sortie and return with wounds, pay and a growing reputation. While the retinue is away, patrols on the coast road are stretched thin.

events.title: THE SOLDIER’S ROAD · THE ROAD WHERE NOTHING HAPPENED
events.text: The patrol reports record a quiet season. Four villages behind the road have brought their goods safely to market, with no great battle for a chronicler to celebrate.

choices.label: Keep the road

outcome.text: You renew the watch and train a capable deputy. The garrison recognises your steady command, even if a safe road makes a poor tale at a feast.

events.title: THE SOLDIER’S ROAD · A NAME THAT TRAVELS
events.text: The name goes further than you ever did and comes home ahead of you. It is worth a great deal in every hall in the shire and nothing at all on the coast road.

choices.label: Live on the name

outcome.text: Your name brings invitations, gifts and a comfortable seat at the next feast. Everyone wants to hear about those same six minutes.

events.title: A MATTER OF JUSTICE · THE FIRST COURT YOU HOLD
events.text: someone once known in Swineford sets the first roll in front of you. Fourteen presentments, four of them against people who cannot read the charge, and every judgement you give today could become a precedent for later hearings.

choices.label: Have every charge read out in English first

outcome.text: It doubles the length of the court and it means every man amerced knows what for. The steward finds it eccentric and it becomes the custom of the manor.

choices.label: Get through the roll efficiently

outcome.text: Sixteen presentments in ninety minutes and four shillings in amercements. It is a well-run court and four men leave it without knowing why they were fined.

events.title: A MATTER OF JUSTICE · THE HERIOT ON A POOR HOLDING
events.text: A tenant dies leaving a widow, four children and one cow. The heriot is the best beast, which is the cow, and it is entirely lawful and it will finish them.

choices.label: Take a token heriot and leave the cow

outcome.text: You take twopence and a pot and enter it in the roll as the best beast. The steward writes it exactly as you dictate and does not look up.

choices.label: Take the cow

outcome.text: The cow comes to the hall. It is lawful, it is what the custom says, and the widow is at her brother’s within the year.

events.title: A MATTER OF JUSTICE · A KNIGHT OF YOUR OWN AFFINITY IS GUILTY
events.text: One of your own retainers has done the thing he is accused of. someone once known in Swineford says the county is watching to see whether your court applies to your own men.

choices.label: Try him in your own court and convict him

outcome.text: He is convicted, fined heavily and put out of the affinity. Three other retainers leave with him and every tenant in the honour hears about it inside a week.

choices.label: Have it settled elsewhere

outcome.text: It goes away through a friend at the assize. The retainer is loyal for life, the county notices, and every man who pleads before you afterwards knows what your court is worth.

events.title: A MATTER OF JUSTICE · THE COMMISSION OF THE PEACE
events.text: You are offered a place on the commission of the peace for the whole shire: real jurisdiction, real work, and every gentleman in the county watching how you use it.

choices.label: Take it and sit at every session

outcome.text: You attend the session, question doubtful charges and insist that the clerk records each ruling. Prisoners receive a fairer hearing and the shire notices your diligence.

choices.label: Take it and use it

outcome.text: The commission is a lever and you use it as one. Favourable settlements enrich your household and strengthen your holding, while the shire questions your impartiality.

events.title: A MATTER OF JUSTICE · THE CUSTOM OF THE MANOR
events.text: The court roll of your honour is quoted in three neighbouring shires as the way it ought to be done. Your lands are worth less than they might be and they are extremely quiet.

choices.label: Keep sitting

outcome.text: You enter the procedure in the court roll: tenants must hear the charge and be allowed to answer. They leave with greater confidence in your court.

events.title: A MATTER OF JUSTICE · PROFIT AND A REPUTATION
events.text: Your household has grown richer through the commission and the shire is entirely clear about how. Nobody says it at your table and everybody says it at their own.

choices.label: Hold what you have taken

outcome.text: You keep the proceeds and secure your holding. The losing parties lodge their objections, and your tenants are less willing to trust the court.
